answerChoices.D: No premodern general theory of art achieves its purpose unless music is not art.
answerChoices.E: No premodern general theory of art explains any aesthetic features of music that are not shared with painting and sculpture.

stimulus: A government ought to protect and encourage free speech, because free speech is an activity that is conducive to a healthy nation and thus is in the best interest of its people.
questionStem: The main conclusion above follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: An activity that is in the best interest of the people ought to be protected and encouraged by a nation's government.
answerChoices.B: Basic, inalienable rights of the people ought to be protected and encouraged by government.
answerChoices.C: An activity that helps a government to govern ought to be protected and encouraged by it.
answerChoices.D: A government ought to protect and encourage an activity that is conducive to the interests of that government.
answerChoices.E: Universal human rights that are in the best interest of the people ought to be protected and encouraged by a nation's government.

stimulus: Manuscripts written by first-time authors generally do not get serious attention by publishers except when these authors happen to be celebrities. My manuscript is unlikely to be taken seriously by publishers for I am a first-time author who is not a celebrity.
questionStem: The structure of which one of the following arguments is most similar to the structure of the argument above?

answerChoices.A: Challengers generally do not win elections unless the incumbent has become very unpopular. The incumbent in this election has become very unpopular. Therefore, the challenger may win.
answerChoices.B: Fruit salad that contains bananas is ordinarily a boring dish unless it contains two or more exotic fruits. This fruit salad has bananas in it, and the only exotic fruit it has is guava. Thus, it will probably be boring.
answerChoices.C: Thursday's city council meeting is likely to be poorly attended. Traditionally, council meetings are sparsely attended if zoning issues are the only ones on the agenda. The agenda for Thursday is exclusively devoted to zoning.
answerChoices.D: The bulk of an estate generally goes to the spouse, if surviving, and otherwise goes to the surviving children. In this case there is no surviving spouse; hence the bulk of the estate is likely to go to the surviving children.
answerChoices.E: Normally about 40 percent of the deer population will die over the winter unless it is extremely mild. The percentage of the deer population that died over the recent winter was the normal 40 percent. I conclude that the recent winter was not unusually mild.

stimulus: People who have political power tend to see new technologies as a means of extending or protecting their power, whereas they generally see new ethical arguments and ideas as a threat to it. Therefore, technical ingenuity usually brings benefits to those who have this ingenuity, whereas ethical inventiveness brings only pain to those who have this inventiveness.
questionStem: Which one of the following statements, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Those who offer new ways of justifying current political power often reap the benefits of their own innovations.
answerChoices.B: Politically powerful people tend to reward those who they believe are useful to them and to punish those who they believe are a threat.
answerChoices.C: Ethical inventiveness and technical ingenuity are never possessed by the same individuals.
answerChoices.D: New technologies are often used by people who strive to defeat those who currently have political power.
answerChoices.E: Many people who possess ethical inventiveness conceal their novel ethical arguments for fear of retribution by the politically powerful.

stimulus: The solidity of bridge piers built on pilings depends largely on how deep the pilings are driven. Prior to 1700, pilings were driven to "refusal," that is, to the point at which they refused to go any deeper. In a 1588 inquiry into the solidity of piers for Venice's Rialto Bridge, it was determined that the bridge's builder, Antonio Da Ponte, had met the contemporary standard for refusal: he had caused the pilings to be driven until additional penetration into the ground was no greater than two inches after twenty-four hammer blows.
questionStem: Which one of the following can properly be inferred from the passage?

answerChoices.A: The Rialto Bridge was built on unsafe pilings.
answerChoices.B: The standard of refusal was not sufficient to ensure the safety of a bridge.
answerChoices.C: Da Ponte's standard of refusal was less strict than that of other bridge builders of his day.
answerChoices.D: After 1588, no bridges were built on pilings that were driven to the point of refusal.
answerChoices.E: It is possible that the pilings of the Rialto Bridge could have been driven deeper even after the standard of refusal had been met.

stimulus: Compared to us, people who lived a century ago had very few diversions to amuse them. Therefore, they likely read much more than we do today.
questionStem: Which one of the following statements, if true, most weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: Many of the books published a century ago were of low literary quality.
answerChoices.B: On average, people who lived a century ago had considerably less leisure time than we do today.
answerChoices.C: The number of books sold today is larger than it was a century ago.
answerChoices.D: On the average, books today cost slightly less in relation to other goods than they did a century ago.
answerChoices.E: One of the popular diversions of a century ago was horse racing.

stimulus: Although consciousness seems to arise from physical processes, physical theories can explain only why physical systems have certain physical structures and how these systems perform various physical functions. Thus, no strictly physical theory can explain consciousness.
questionStem: The conclusion of the argument follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Physical theories can explain only physical phenomena.
answerChoices.B: An explanation of consciousness must encompass more than an explanation of physical structures and functions.
answerChoices.C: The physical structures and functions of consciousness are currently unknown.
answerChoices.D: Consciousness arises from processes that are entirely explainable by physical theories.
answerChoices.E: An explanation of physical structures and functions must be formulated in strictly physical terms.

stimulus: Rosen: One cannot prepare a good meal from bad food, produce good food from bad soil, maintain good soil without good farming, or have good farming without a culture that places value on the proper maintenance of all its natural resources so that needed supplies are always available.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from Rosen's statement?

answerChoices.A: The creation of good meals depends on both natural and cultural conditions.
answerChoices.B: Natural resources cannot be maintained properly without good farming practices.
answerChoices.C: Good soil is a prerequisite of good farming.
answerChoices.D: Any society with good cultural values will have a good cuisine.
answerChoices.E: When food is bad, it is because of poor soil and, ultimately, bad farming practices.

stimulus: A safety report indicates that, on average, traffic fatalities decline by about 7 percent in those areas in which strict laws requiring drivers and passengers to wear seat belts have been passed. In a certain city, seat belt laws have been in effect for two years, but the city's public safety records show that the number of traffic deaths per year has remained the same.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, does not help resolve the apparent discrepancy between the safety report and the city's public safety records?

answerChoices.A: Two years ago speed limits in the city were increased by as much as 15 kph (9 mph).
answerChoices.B: The city now includes pedestrian fatalities in its yearly total of traffic deaths, whereas two years ago it did not.
answerChoices.C: In the time since the seat belt laws were passed, the city has experienced a higher than average increase in automobile traffic.
answerChoices.D: Because the city's seat belt laws have been so rarely enforced, few drivers in the city have complied with them.
answerChoices.E: In the last two years, most of the people killed in car accidents in the city were not wearing seat belts.

stimulus: The studies showing that increased consumption of fruits and vegetables may help decrease the incidence of some types of cancer do not distinguish between organically grown and nonorganically grown produce; they were conducted with produce at least some of which contained pesticide residues. The studies may also be taken as showing, therefore, that there is no increased health risk associated with eating fruits and vegetables containing pesticide residues.
questionStem: The pattern of flawed reasoning in which one of the following is most similar to the pattern of flawed reasoning in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: Research shows that the incidence of certain major illnesses, including heart disease and cancer, is decreased in communities that have a modern power plant. The fact that this tendency is present whether the power plant is nuclear or not shows that there is no increased health risk associated with living next to a nuclear power plant.
answerChoices.B: Research has shown that there is no long-term health risk associated with a diet consisting largely of foods high in saturated fat and cholesterol if such a diet is consumed by someone with a physically active lifestyle. So, exercise is a more useful strategy for achieving cardiological health than is dietary restriction.
answerChoices.C: Research has shown that young people who drive motorcycles and receive one full year of extensive driving instruction are in fact less likely to become involved in accidents than those who simply pass a driving test and drive cars. This shows that there is not an inherently greater risk associated with driving a motorcycle than with driving a car.
answerChoices.D: Research has shown that kitchen cutting boards retain significant numbers of microbes even after careful washing, but that after washing fewer microbes are found on wooden boards than on plastic boards. There is, therefore, no greater risk of contracting microbial illnesses associated with using wooden cutting boards than with using plastic cutting boards.
answerChoices.E: Research shows that there is no greater long-term health benefit associated with taking vitamin supplements than with a moderate increase in the intake of fruits and vegetables. Clearly, then, there is no long-term health risk associated with the failure to take vitamin supplements, so long as enough fruits and vegetables are consumed.

stimulus: I agree that Hogan's actions resulted in grievous injury to Winters. And I do not deny that Hogan fully realized the nature of his actions and the effects that they would have. Indeed, I would not disagree if you pointed out that intentionally causing such effects is reprehensible, other things being equal. But in asking you to concur with me that Hogan's actions not be wholly condemned I emphasize again that Hogan mistakenly believed Winters to be the robber who had been terrorizing west-side apartment buildings for the past several months.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the conclusion of the argument?

answerChoices.A: Hogan should not be considered responsible for the injuries sustained by Winters.
answerChoices.B: The robber who had been terrorizing west-side apartment buildings should be considered to be as responsible for Winters's injuries as Hogan.
answerChoices.C: The actions of Hogan that seriously injured Winters are not completely blameworthy.
answerChoices.D: Hogan thought that Winters was the person who had been terrorizing west-side apartment buildings for the last few months.
answerChoices.E: The actions of Hogan that seriously injured Winters were reprehensible, other things being equal.

stimulus:
Peter: Because the leaves of mildly drought-stressed plants are tougher in texture than the leaves of abundantly watered plants, insects prefer to feed on the leaves of abundantly watered plants. Therefore, to minimize crop damage, farmers should water crops only just enough to ensure that there is no substantial threat, from a lack of water, to either the growth or the yield of the crops.
Jennifer: Indeed. In fact, a mildly drought-stressed plant will divert a small amount of its resources from normal growth to the development of pesticidal toxins, but abundantly watered plants will not.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens Peter's argument?

answerChoices.A: The leaves of some crop plants are much larger, and therefore absorb more water, than the leaves of some other crop plants.
answerChoices.B: In industrialized nations there are more crops that are abundantly watered than there are crops grown under mild drought stress.
answerChoices.C: Insect damage presents a greater threat to crop plants than does mild drought stress.
answerChoices.D: Farmers are not always able to control the amount of water that their crops receive when, for instance, there are rainstorms in the areas where their crops are growing.
answerChoices.E: Mexican bean beetles are more likely to feed on the leaves of slightly drought-stressed soybeans than oak lace bugs are to feed on the leaves of abundantly watered soybeans.

stimulus: While it was once believed that the sort of psychotherapy appropriate for the treatment of neuroses caused by environmental factors is also appropriate for schizophrenia and other psychoses, it is now known that these latter, more serious forms of mental disturbance are best treated by biochemical-that is, medicinal-means. This is conclusive evidence that psychoses, unlike neuroses, have nothing to do with environmental factors but rather are caused by some sort of purely organic condition, such as abnormal brain chemistry or brain malformations.
questionStem: The argument is vulnerable to criticism because it ignores the possibility that

answerChoices.A: the organic conditions that result in psychoses can be caused or exacerbated by environmental factors
answerChoices.B: the symptoms of mental disturbance caused by purely organic factors can be alleviated with medicine
answerChoices.C: organic illnesses that are nonpsychological in nature may be treatable without using biochemical methods
answerChoices.D: the nature of any medical condition can be inferred from the nature of the treatment that cures that condition
answerChoices.E: organic factors having little to do with brain chemistry may be at least partially responsible for neuroses

stimulus: It is said that people should accept themselves as they are instead of being dissatisfied with their own abilities. But this is clearly a bad principle if the goal is a society whose citizens are genuinely happy, for no one can be genuinely happy if he or she is not pursuing personal excellence and is unwilling to undergo personal change of any kind.
questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument?

answerChoices.A: Those who are willing to change will probably find genuine happiness.
answerChoices.B: People who are not dissatisfied with themselves are less likely than others to pursue personal excellence.
answerChoices.C: Personal excellence cannot be acquired by those who lack genuine confidence in their own abilities.
answerChoices.D: People are justified in feeling content with themselves when they have achieved some degree of personal excellence.
answerChoices.E: Happiness is not genuine unless it is based on something that is painful to obtain.

stimulus: My father likes turnips, but not potatoes, which he says are tasteless. So it is not true that whoever likes potatoes likes turnips.
questionStem: The flawed reasoning in the argument above most closely resembles that in which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: This book is not a paperback, but it is expensive. So it is not true that some paperbacks are expensive.
answerChoices.B: Although this recently published work of fiction has more than 75 pages, it is not a novel. Thus, it is not the case that all novels have more than 75 pages.
answerChoices.C: All ornate buildings were constructed before the twentieth century. This house is ornate, so it must be true that it was built before the twentieth century.
answerChoices.D: Erica enjoys studying physics, but not pure mathematics, which she says is boring. So it is not true that whoever enjoys studying physics enjoys studying pure mathematics.
answerChoices.E: People who do their own oil changes are car fanatics. My next-door neighbors are car fanatics, so it follows that they do their own oil changes.

stimulus: Critic: Although some people claim it is inconsistent to support freedom of speech and also support legislation limiting the amount of violence in TV programs, it is not. We can limit TV program content because the damage done by violent programs is more harmful than the decrease in freedom of speech that would result from the limitations envisioned by the legislation.
questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the critic's reasoning?

answerChoices.A: In evaluating legislation that would impinge on a basic freedom, we should consider the consequences of not passing the legislation.
answerChoices.B: One can support freedom of speech while at the same time recognizing that it can sometimes be overridden by other interests.
answerChoices.C: When facing a choice between restricting freedom of speech or not, we must decide based on what would make the greatest number of people the happiest.
answerChoices.D: If the exercise of a basic freedom leads to some harm, then the exercise of that freedom should be restricted.
answerChoices.E: In some circumstances, we should tolerate regulations that impinge on a basic freedom.

stimulus: Anthropologist: All music is based on a few main systems of scale building. Clearly, if the popularity of a musical scale were a result of social conditioning, we would expect, given the diversity of social systems, a diverse mixture of diatonic and nondiatonic scales in the world's music. Yet diatonic scales have always dominated the music of most of the world. Therefore, the popularity of diatonic music can be attributed only to innate dispositions of the human mind.
questionStem: The anthropologist's argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it fails to

answerChoices.A: consider the possibility that some people appreciate nondiatonic music more than they do diatonic music
answerChoices.B: explain how innate dispositions increase appreciation of nondiatonic music
answerChoices.C: explain the existence of diatonic scales as well as the existence of nondiatonic scales
answerChoices.D: consider that innate dispositions and social conditioning could jointly affect the popularity of a type of music
answerChoices.E: consider whether any appreciation of nondiatonic music is demonstrated by some nonhuman species of animals

stimulus: Before 1986 physicists believed they could describe the universe in terms of four universal forces. Experiments then suggested, however, a fifth universal force of mutual repulsion between particles of matter. This fifth force would explain the occurrence in the experiments of a smaller measurement of the gravitational attraction between bodies than the established theory predicted.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument that there is a fifth universal force?

answerChoices.A: The extremely sophisticated equipment used for the experiments was not available to physicists before the 1970s.
answerChoices.B: No previously established scientific results are incompatible with the notion of a fifth universal force.
answerChoices.C: Some scientists have suggested that the alleged fifth universal force is an aspect of gravity rather than being fundamental in itself.
answerChoices.D: The experiments were conducted by physicists in remote geological settings in which factors affecting the force of gravity could not be measured with any degree of precision.
answerChoices.E: The fifth universal force was postulated at a time in which many other exciting and productive ideas in theoretical physics were developed.

stimulus: The vomeronasal organ (VNO) is found inside the noses of various animals. While its structural development and function are clearer in other animals, most humans have a VNO that is detectable, though only microscopically. When researchers have been able to stimulate VNO cells in humans, the subjects have reported experiencing subtle smell sensations. It seems, then, that the VNO, though not completely understood, is a functioning sensory organ in most humans.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: It is not known whether the researchers succeeded in stimulating only VNO cells in the human subjects' noses.
answerChoices.B: Relative to its occurrence in certain other animals, the human VNO appears to be anatomically rudimentary and underdeveloped.
answerChoices.C: Certain chemicals that play a leading role in the way the VNO functions in animals in which it is highly developed do not appear to play a role in its functioning in humans.
answerChoices.D: Secondary anatomical structures associated with the VNO in other animals seem to be absent in humans.
answerChoices.E: For many animal species, the VNO is thought to subtly enhance the sense of smell.

stimulus: After 1950, in response to record growth in worldwide food demand, farmers worldwide sharply increased fertilizer use. As a result, the productivity of farmland more than doubled by 1985. Since 1985, farmers have sought to increase farmland productivity even further. Nevertheless, worldwide fertilizer use has declined by 6 percent between 1985 and the present.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

answerChoices.A: Since 1985 the rate at which the world's population has increased has exceeded the rate at which new arable land has been created through irrigation and other methods.
answerChoices.B: Several varieties of crop plants that have become popular recently, such as soybeans, are as responsive to fertilizer as are traditional grain crops.
answerChoices.C: Between 1950 and 1985 farmers were able to increase the yield of many varieties of crop plants.
answerChoices.D: After fertilizer has been added to soil for several years, adding fertilizer to the soil in subsequent years does not significantly improve crop production.
answerChoices.E: Between 1975 and 1980 fertilizer prices temporarily increased because of labor disputes in several fertilizer-exporting nations, and these disputes disrupted worldwide fertilizer production.

stimulus: Cultural historian: Universal acceptance of scientific theories that regard human beings only as natural objects subject to natural forces outside the individual's control will inevitably lead to a general decline in morality. After all, if people do not believe that they are responsible for their actions, they will feel unashamed when they act immorally, and a widespread failure of individuals to feel ashamed of their immoral actions is bound to lead to a general moral decline.
questionStem: The conclusion drawn by the cultural historian follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Science does not enable human beings to control natural forces.
answerChoices.B: Human beings who regard themselves only as natural objects will as a result lose their sense of responsibility for their actions.
answerChoices.C: People who have a sense of shame for their moral transgressions will feel responsible for their actions.
answerChoices.D: Some scientific theories hold that human beings are not responsible for their actions.
answerChoices.E: Scientific explanations that regard human beings as in some respects independent of the laws of nature will not lead to a general decline in morality.

stimulus: A year ago the government reduced the highway speed limit, and in the year since, there have been significantly fewer highway fatalities than there were in the previous year. Therefore, speed limit reduction can reduce traffic fatalities.
questionStem: The argument is most vulnerable to the criticism that it takes for granted that

answerChoices.A: highway traffic has not increased over the past year
answerChoices.B: the majority of drivers obeyed the new speed limit
answerChoices.C: there is a relation between driving speed and the number of automobile accidents
answerChoices.D: the new speed limit was more strictly enforced than the old
answerChoices.E: the number of traffic fatalities the year before the new speed limit was introduced was not abnormally high

stimulus: A plausible explanation of the disappearance of the dinosaurs is what is known as the comet theory. A large enough comet colliding with Earth could have caused a cloud of dust that enshrouded the planet and cooled the climate long enough to result in the dinosaurs' demise.
questionStem: Which one of the following statements, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: One of the various schools of paleontology adheres to an explanation for the disappearance of the dinosaurs that is significantly different from the comet theory.
answerChoices.B: Various species of animals from the same era as the dinosaurs and similar to them in physiology and habitat did not become extinct when the dinosaurs did.
answerChoices.C: It cannot be determined from a study of dinosaur skeletons whether the animals died from the effects of a dust cloud.
answerChoices.D: Many other animal species from the era of the dinosaurs did not become extinct at the same time the dinosaurs did.
answerChoices.E: The consequences for vegetation and animals of a comet colliding with Earth are not fully understood.

stimulus: In ancient Mesopotamia, prior to 2900 B.C., wheat was cultivated in considerable quantities, but after 2900 B.C. production of that grain began to decline as the production of barley increased sharply. Some historians who study ancient Mesopotamia contend that the decline in wheat production was due to excessive irrigation, lack of drainage, and the consequent accumulation of salt residues in the soil.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to support the historians' contention concerning the reasons for the decline in wheat production in ancient Mesopotamia?

answerChoices.A: The cultivation of barley requires considerably less water than does the cultivation of wheat.
answerChoices.B: Barley has much greater resistance to the presence of salt in soil than does wheat.
answerChoices.C: Prior to 2900 B.C., barley was cultivated along with wheat, but the amount of barley produced was far less than the amount of wheat produced.
answerChoices.D: Around 2900 B.C., a series of wheat blights occurred, destroying much of the wheat crop year after year.
answerChoices.E: Literary and archaeological evidence indicates that in the period following 2900 B.C., barley became the principal grain in the diet of most of the inhabitants of Mesopotamia.

stimulus: Physician: In itself, exercise does not cause heart attacks; rather, a sudden increase in an exercise regimen can be a cause. When people of any physical condition suddenly increase their amount of exercise, they also increase their risk of heart attack. As a result, there will be an increased risk of heart attack among employees of this company due to the new health program.
questionStem: The conclusion drawn by the physician follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Employees will abruptly increase their amount of exercise as a result of the new health program.
answerChoices.B: The exercises involved in the new health program are more strenuous than those in the previous health program.
answerChoices.C: The new health program will force employees of all levels of health to exercise regularly.
answerChoices.D: The new health program constitutes a sudden change in the company's policy.
answerChoices.E: All employees, no matter what their physical condition, will participate in the new health program.

stimulus: Mystery stories often feature a brilliant detective and the detective's dull companion. Clues are presented in the story, and the companion wrongly infers an inaccurate solution to the mystery using the same clues that the detective uses to deduce the correct solution. Thus, the author's strategy of including the dull companion gives readers a chance to solve the mystery while also diverting them from the correct solution.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Most mystery stories feature a brilliant detective who solves the mystery presented in the story.
answerChoices.B: Mystery readers often solve the mystery in a story simply by spotting the mistakes in the reasoning of the detective's dull companion in that story.
answerChoices.C: Some mystery stories give readers enough clues to infer the correct solution to the mystery.
answerChoices.D: The actions of the brilliant detective in a mystery story rarely divert readers from the actions of the detective's dull companion.
answerChoices.E: The detective's dull companion in a mystery story generally uncovers the misleading clues that divert readers from the mystery's correct solution.

stimulus: In order to determine automobile insurance premiums for a driver, insurance companies calculate various risk factors; as the risk factors increase, so does the premium. Certain factors, such as the driver's age and past accident history, play an important role in these calculations. Yet these premiums should also increase with the frequency with which a person drives. After all, a person's chance of being involved in a mishap increases in proportion to the number of times that person drives.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most undermines the argument?

answerChoices.A: People who drive infrequently are more likely to be involved in accidents that occur on small roads than in highway accidents.
answerChoices.B: People who drive infrequently are less likely to follow rules for safe driving than are people who drive frequently.
answerChoices.C: People who drive infrequently are less likely to violate local speed limits than are people who drive frequently.
answerChoices.D: People who drive frequently are more likely to make long-distance trips in the course of a year than are people who drive infrequently.
answerChoices.E: People who drive frequently are more likely to become distracted while driving than are people who drive infrequently.

stimulus: Essayist: Only happiness is intrinsically valuable; other things are valuable only insofar as they contribute to happiness. Some philosophers argue that the fact that we do not approve of a bad person's being happy shows that we value happiness only when it is deserved. This supposedly shows that we find something besides happiness to be intrinsically valuable. But the happiness people deserve is determined by the amount of happiness they bring to others. Therefore,
questionStem: Which one of the following most logically completes the final sentence of the essayist's argument?

answerChoices.A: the notion that people can be deserving of happiness is ultimately incoherent
answerChoices.B: people do not actually value happiness as much as they think they do
answerChoices.C: the judgment that a person deserves to be happy is itself to be understood in terms of happiness
answerChoices.D: the only way to be assured of happiness is to bring happiness to those who have done something to deserve it
answerChoices.E: a truly bad person cannot actually be very happy

stimulus: Sociologist: Climate and geology determine where human industry can be established. Drastic shifts in climate always result in migrations, and migrations bring about the intermingling of ideas necessary for rapid advances in civilization.
questionStem: The sociologist's statements, if true, most strongly support which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Climate is the primary cause of migration.
answerChoices.B: All shifts in climate produce a net gain in human progress.
answerChoices.C: A population remains settled only where the climate is fairly stable.
answerChoices.D: Populations settle in every place where human industry can be established.
answerChoices.E: Every migration is accompanied by rapid advances in civilization.

stimulus: Some educators claim that it is best that school courses cover only basic subject matter, but cover it in depth. These educators argue that if students achieve a solid grasp of the basic concepts and investigatory techniques in a subject, they will be able to explore the breadth of that subject on their own after the course is over. But if they simply learn a lot of factual information, without truly understanding its significance, they will not be well equipped for further study on their own.
questionStem: The educators' reasoning provides grounds for accepting which one of the following statements?

answerChoices.A: It is easier to understand how plants and animals are classified after learning how plants and animals can be useful.
answerChoices.B: It is more difficult to recall the details of a dull and complicated lecture than of a lively and interesting one.
answerChoices.C: It is easier to remember new ideas explained personally by a teacher than ideas that one explores independently.
answerChoices.D: It is easier to understand any Greek tragedy after one has analyzed a few of them in detail.
answerChoices.E: It is easier to learn many simple ideas well than to learn a few complicated ideas well.

stimulus: One thousand people in Denmark were questioned about their views on banning cigarette advertising. The sample comprised adults who are representative of the general population, and who, ten years previously, had been questioned on the same issue. Interestingly, their opinions changed little. Results show that 31 percent are in favor of such a ban, 24 percent are against it, 38 percent are in favor, but only for certain media, and 7 percent have no opinion.
questionStem: The survey results in the passage best support which one of the following conclusions?

answerChoices.A: People's opinions never change very much.
answerChoices.B: A minority of Denmark's population feels that banning cigarette advertising would set a bad precedent.
answerChoices.C: Most of Denmark's population is not seriously concerned about cigarette advertising.
answerChoices.D: Most of Denmark's population favors some sort of ban on cigarette advertising.
answerChoices.E: Most of Denmark's population does not smoke cigarettes.

stimulus: Passenger volume in the airline industry has declined dramatically over the past two years, and thus fewer travelers and fewer planes are using airports. Since airport expansion can be warranted only by increases in air traffic volume, and since it will probably be at least five years before passenger volume returns to and then exceeds its previous level, it seems surprising that now is the time that airports are going ahead with plans to expand their passenger terminal facilities.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, provides the best reason in favor of the airports' timing of their planned expansions?

answerChoices.A: It is generally more difficult to finance major construction projects when the economy is in a period of decline.
answerChoices.B: Low volume in passenger air travel permits airport expansion with relatively little inconvenience to the public.
answerChoices.C: A rise in fuel costs that is expected in the near future will drive up the cost of all forms of transportation, including airline travel.
answerChoices.D: When passenger volume begins to grow again after a period of decline, most airlines can, initially, absorb the increase without adding new routes or new planes.
answerChoices.E: A sustained decline in passenger travel could lead to the failure of many airlines and the absorption of their routes by those airlines that survive.

stimulus: Books updating the classification systems used by many libraries are not free—in fact they are very expensive. The only way to sell copies of them is to make the potential buyers believe they need to adopt the most recent system. Thus, these frequent changes in the classification systems are just a ploy by the publishers to make libraries buy their products.
questionStem: The reasoning above is most vulnerable to criticism because it

answerChoices.A: claims without providing warrant that the books are unreasonably expensive
answerChoices.B: concludes that a possible ulterior motive must be the only motive
answerChoices.C: fails to consider that there may be potential buyers of these books other than libraries
answerChoices.D: concludes that there is no need ever to change classification systems
answerChoices.E: fails to consider that the libraries cannot afford to buy every book they want

stimulus:
Ashley: Words like "of" and "upon," unlike "pencil" and "shirt," do not refer to anything.
Joshua: I agree; and since such words are meaningless, they should be abandoned.
questionStem: Joshua's remarks indicate that he interpreted Ashley's statement to imply that

answerChoices.A: only words that refer to something have meaning
answerChoices.B: words that are not useful are meaningless
answerChoices.C: words that refer to something are meaningful
answerChoices.D: if a word is not useful, it should be abandoned
answerChoices.E: all words that refer to something are useful

stimulus: Ethicist: Some would ban cloning on the grounds that clones would be subpeople, existing to indulge the vanity of their "originals." It is not illegal, however, to use one person as a vehicle for the ambitions of another. Some people push their children to achieve in academics or athletics. You do not have to have been born in a test tube to be an extension of someone else's ego.
questionStem: The assertion that it is not illegal to use one person as a vehicle for another's ambitions is used in the ethicist's argument in which one of the following ways?

answerChoices.A: It supports the ethicist's view that society does not value individuality as much as many opponents of cloning think it does.
answerChoices.B: It supports the conclusion that forcing children to pursue academic success is not objectionable.
answerChoices.C: It is implied by the ethicist's conviction that clones are not subpeople.
answerChoices.D: It supports the ethicist's view that vanity's being the motivation for cloning is not enough of a reason to ban cloning.
answerChoices.E: It describes a legal position that the ethicist argues should be changed.

stimulus: Appliance dealer: Appliance manufacturers commonly modify existing models without giving the modified versions new model names. Some people have complained that this practice makes it impossible for consumers to be certain that the appliance they are about to purchase is identical to the one they may have seen at a neighbor's or read about in a consumer magazine. Yet manufacturers' modifications to existing models are invariably improvements that benefit the buyer. Therefore, consumers have little reason to object to this practice.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the dealer's argument?

answerChoices.A: Appliances are generally purchased with the expectation that they will continue to be used for several years.
answerChoices.B: Appliances usually carry a model number that provides substantially more detailed information about the product than does the model name.
answerChoices.C: Appliance manufacturers frequently sell identical products under several different model names.
answerChoices.D: Improved versions of appliances typically become available before vendors have stopped selling the older versions of the appliance with the same model name.
answerChoices.E: The high cost of product advertising makes appliance manufacturers generally reluctant to change model names to reflect modifications to their products.

stimulus: The following passage is used for Section 4, questions 1 through 2. Ms. Smith: I am upset that my son’s entire class lost two days of recess because some of the children were throwing raisins in the cafeteria. He was not throwing raisins, and it was clear to everyone just who the culprits were. Principal: I’m sorry you’re upset, Ms. Smith, but your son’s situation is like being caught in a traffic jam caused by an accident. People who aren’t involved in the accident nevertheless have to suffer by sitting there in the middle of it.
questionStem: 1. If the principal is speaking sincerely, then it can be inferred from what the principal says that the principal believes that

answerChoices.A: many children were throwing raisins in the cafeteria
answerChoices.B: Ms. Smith’s son might not have thrown raisins in the cafeteria
answerChoices.C: after an accident the resulting traffic jams are generally caused by police activity
answerChoices.D: Ms. Smith’s son knows who it was that threw raisins in the cafeteria
answerChoices.E: losing two days of recess will deter future disruptions

stimulus: Loggerhead turtles live and breed in distinct groups, of which some are in the Pacific Ocean and some are in the Atlantic. New evidence suggests that juvenile Pacific loggerheads that feed near the Baja peninsula hatch in Japanese waters 10,000 kilometers away. Ninety-five percent of the DNA samples taken from the Baja turtles match those taken from turtles at the Japanese nesting sites.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: Nesting sites of loggerhead turtles have been found off the Pacific coast of North America several thousand kilometers north of the Baja peninsula.
answerChoices.B: The distance between nesting sites and feeding sites of Atlantic loggerhead turtles is less than 5,000 kilometers.
answerChoices.C: Loggerhead hatchlings in Japanese waters have been declining in number for the last decade while the number of nesting sites near the Baja peninsula has remained constant.
answerChoices.D: Ninety-five percent of the DNA samples taken from the Baja turtles match those taken from Atlantic loggerhead turtles.
answerChoices.E: Commercial aquariums have been successfully breeding Atlantic loggerheads with Pacific loggerheads for the last five years.

stimulus: People who do not believe that others distrust them are confident in their own abilities, so people who tend to trust others think of a difficult task as a challenge rather than a threat, since this is precisely how people who are confident in their own abilities regard such tasks.
questionStem: The conclusion above follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: People who believe that others distrust them tend to trust others.
answerChoices.B: Confidence in one’s own abilities gives one confidence in the trustworthiness of others.
answerChoices.C: People who tend to trust others do not believe that others distrust them.
answerChoices.D: People who are not threatened by difficult tasks tend to find such tasks challenging.
answerChoices.E: People tend to distrust those who they believe lack self-confidence.

stimulus: Mullen has proposed to raise taxes on the rich, who made so much money during the past decade. Yet Mullen’s tax records show heavy investment in business during that time and large profits; so Mullen’s proposal does not deserve our consideration. The flawed reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the flawed reasoning in which one of the
questionStem: following?

answerChoices.A: Do not vote for Smith’s proposed legislation to subsidize child care for working parents; Smith is a working parent.
answerChoices.B: Do not put any credence in Dr. Han’s recent proposal to ban smoking in all public places; Dr. Han is a heavy smoker.
answerChoices.C: The previous witness’s testimony ought to be ignored; he has been convicted of both forgery and mail fraud.
answerChoices.D: Board member Timm’s proposal to raise the salaries of the company’s middle managers does not deserve to be considered; Timm’s daughter is a middle manager at the company’s headquarters.
answerChoices.E: Dr. Wasow’s analysis of the design of this bridge should not be taken seriously; after all, Dr. Wasow has previously only designed factory buildings.

stimulus: The following passage is used for Section 4, questions 18 through 19. Anders: The physical structure of the brain plays an important role in thinking. So researchers developing “thinking machines”—computers that can make decisions based on both common sense and factual knowledge—should closely model those machines on the structure of the brain. Yang: Important does not mean essential. After all, no flying machine closely modeled on birds has worked; workable aircraft are structurally very different from birds. So thinking machines closely modeled on the brain are also likely to fail. In developing a workable thinking machine, researchers would therefore increase their chances of success if they focus on the brain’s function and simply ignore its physical structure.
questionStem: 19.	 In evaluating Yang’s argument it would be most helpful to know whether

answerChoices.A: studies of the physical structure of birds provided information crucial to the development of workable aircraft
answerChoices.B: researchers currently working on thinking machines take all thinking to involve both common sense and factual knowledge
answerChoices.C: as much time has been spent trying to develop a workable thinking machine as had been spent in developing the first workable aircraft
answerChoices.D: researchers who specialize in the structure of the brain are among those who are trying to develop thinking machines
answerChoices.E: some flying machines that were not closely modeled on birds failed to work

stimulus: Letter to the editor: Allowing everyone to voice personal views can have the effect of inhibiting some from voicing their concerns. Thus, allowing unrestricted free speech really inhibits free speech.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, does most to justify the apparently contradictory conclusion above?

answerChoices.A: When free speech is unrestricted, many people will be shocked by the power of the views of others and thereby become afraid to voice their own concerns.
answerChoices.B: When there is unrestricted free speech, there will be a greater number of diverse views expressed, but the views expressed will be potentially offensive to many people.
answerChoices.C: Since unrestricted free speech can be offensive, free speech should be restricted when the pain that it causes is great.
answerChoices.D: Claiming that unrestricted free speech inhibits free speech is like claiming that increasing someone's salary makes the person poorer.
answerChoices.E: When free speech is unrestricted, people offended by the views of others are likely to voice their disagreement, leading toward a resolution of conflict.

stimulus: Lactose, a sugar found in milk, aids in the absorption of calcium, which in turn is required for bone repair. In addition to there being shortages of milk in tropical areas, inhabitants of these areas lose the ability to absorb lactose, unlike people from nontropical areas. Yet inhabitants of tropical areas have no more problems with bone repair than do people who inhabit nontropical areas.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox described above?

answerChoices.A: People living in tropical areas periodically take tablets containing lactose when there are shortages of milk.
answerChoices.B: Milk consumption has fallen in both tropical and nontropical areas.
answerChoices.C: The abundant sunlight in tropical areas causes the human body to produce vitamin D naturally, which aids in the absorption of calcium.
answerChoices.D: Consumption of dairy products other than milk has risen slightly in tropical areas.
answerChoices.E: The extent to which people living in tropical areas lose the ability to absorb lactose depends on a genetic predisposition.

stimulus: A politician can neither be reelected nor avoid censure by his or her colleagues if that politician is known to be involved in any serious scandals. Several prominent politicians have just now been shown to be involved in a conspiracy that turned into a serious scandal. These politicians will therefore not be reelected.
questionStem: If the statements above are all true, which one of the following statements must also be true?

answerChoices.A: The prominent politicians cannot escape censure by their colleagues.
answerChoices.B: If there had been no scandal, the prominent politicians would be reelected.
answerChoices.C: No politician is censured unless he or she is known to be involved in a serious scandal.
answerChoices.D: The prominent politicians initially benefited from the conspiracy that caused the scandal.
answerChoices.E: Some politicians who are involved in scandalous conspiracies avoid detection and censure.

stimulus: In each of the last ten years, there have been few complaints to law enforcement agencies of telemarketing fraud. Yet, in the last ten years, fraudulent telemarketing schemes have become a more and more serious problem, bilking victims out of millions of dollars annually.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent conflict described above?

answerChoices.A: Telemarketers convicted of fraud tend to be punished more severely than other people convicted of nonviolent crimes.
answerChoices.B: Most complaints of telemarketing fraud that authorities investigate involve the use of credit cards, which makes it extremely difficult for law enforcement agencies to track down the perpetrators.
answerChoices.C: Some fraudulent telemarketers have concocted phony investment schemes which make it unlikely that victims will detect the fraud until a year or two after the fact, by which time their swindlers are long gone.
answerChoices.D: Fraudulent telemarketers typically base their operations outside the legal jurisdiction inhabited by the people they solicit, so they must be prosecuted in higher courts.
answerChoices.E: The majority of those who have been defrauded by telemarketers have been inclined not to seek any legal remedy, out of embarrassment at being duped.

stimulus: Cézanne's art inspired the next generation of artists, twentieth-century modernist creators of abstract art. While most experts rank Cézanne as an early modernist, a small few reject this idea. Françoise Cachin, for example, bluntly states that such an ascription is "overplayed," and says that Cézanne's work is “too often observed from a modern point of view."
questionStem: Which one of the following statements is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Cézanne's work is highly controversial.
answerChoices.B: Cézanne was an early creator of abstract art.
answerChoices.C: Cézanne's work helped to develop modernism.
answerChoices.D: Modern art owes less to Cézanne than many experts believe.
answerChoices.E: Cézanne's work tends to be misinterpreted as modernist.

stimulus: Ecologist: Forest fires, the vast majority of which are started by lightning, are not only a natural phenomenon to which all forest ecosystems are well adapted, but are required for many forests to flourish. Forest fires facilitate the opening and spreading of seed pods, prevent an overabundance of insects, and promote the diversity of forests by preventing certain varieties of aggressive weeds from dominating other species. In view of this, systematic attempts by human beings to prevent or control forest fires are ill-advised and shortsighted; forest fires should be left alone and allowed to burn themselves out naturally.
questionStem: The conclusion drawn above follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Human intervention in natural processes tends to reduce the biological diversity of ecosystems.
answerChoices.B: Protection of forests and their ecosystems is the only legitimate reason for attempting to prevent or control forest fires.
answerChoices.C: Forest fires begun by careless campers should be the target of human fire control efforts.
answerChoices.D: Humans tend to view forests as well as other ecosystems as instruments for the satisfaction of human needs.
answerChoices.E: If the health of an ecosystem is threatened by insects or other predators, human beings should not intervene to block that threat.

stimulus: Editorial: Given the law of supply and demand, maximum total utility is assured only in a pure free market economy, although other types of economies might be able to achieve it. Obviously, then, a country that has a highly controlled economy, and is not trying to bring about a pure free market economy, is not acting in the way that is most likely to bring about maximum total utility.
questionStem: The editorial's argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it

answerChoices.A: presumes, without providing justification, that any country that does not have a pure free market economy has a highly controlled economy
answerChoices.B: presumes, without providing justification, that the way in which utility is distributed is less important than the total amount of utility
answerChoices.C: fails to consider that the way most likely to achieve a particular end may not be the only way to achieve that end
answerChoices.D: presumes, without providing justification, that trying to bring about a condition that will ensure the achievement of an end must always be the way most likely to achieve that end
answerChoices.E: ignores the possibility that a pure free market economy will have serious drawbacks that outweigh the benefits of maximum total utility

stimulus: Kendrick: Governments that try to prevent cigarettes from being advertised are justified in doing so, since such advertisements encourage people to engage in an unhealthy practice. But cigarette advertisements should remain legal since advertisements for fatty foods are legal, even though those advertisements also encourage people to engage in unhealthy practices.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent conflict between Kendrick's statements?

answerChoices.A: Any advertisement that encourages people to engage in an unhealthy practice should be made illegal, even though the legality of some such advertisements is currently uncontroversial.
answerChoices.B: The advertisement of fattening foods, unlike that of cigarettes, should not be prevented, because fattening foods, unlike cigarettes, are not addictive.
answerChoices.C: Most advertisements should be legal, although advertisers are always morally responsible for ensuring that their advertisements do not encourage people to engage in unhealthy practices.
answerChoices.D: Governments should try to prevent the advertisement of cigarettes by means of financial disincentives rather than by legal prohibition.
answerChoices.E: Governments should place restrictions on cigarette advertisements so as to keep them from encouraging people to engage in unhealthy practices, but should not try to prevent such advertisements.

stimulus: The development of new inventions is promoted by the granting of patent rights, which restrict the right of anyone but the patent holders to profit from these inventions for a specified period. Without patent rights, anyone could simply copy another's invention; consequently, inventors would have no financial incentive for investing the time and energy required to develop new products. Thus, it is important to continue to grant patent rights, or else no one will engage in original development and consequently no new inventions will be forthcoming.
questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?

answerChoices.A: Financial reward is the only incentive that will be effective in motivating people to develop new inventions.
answerChoices.B: When an inventor sells patent rights to a manufacturer, the manufacturer makes less total profit on the invention than the inventor does.
answerChoices.C: Any costs incurred by a typical inventor in applying for patent rights are insignificant in comparison to the financial benefit of holding the patent rights.
answerChoices.D: Patent rights should be granted only if an inventor's product is not similar to another invention already covered by patent rights.
answerChoices.E: The length of a patent right is usually proportional to the costs involved in inventing the product.

stimulus: Resident: Residents of this locale should not consider their loss of farming as a way of life to be a tragedy. When this area was a rural area it was economically depressed, but it is now a growing bastion of high-tech industry with high-wage jobs, and supports over 20 times the number of jobs it did then.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, does the most to justify the conclusion of the resident's argument?

answerChoices.A: Farming is becoming increasingly efficient, with the result that fewer farms are required to produce the same amount of food.
answerChoices.B: The development of high-tech industry is more valuable to national security than is farming.
answerChoices.C: Residents of this locale do not value a rural way of life more than they value economic prosperity.
answerChoices.D: Many residents of this locale have annual incomes that are twice what they were when the locale was primarily agricultural.
answerChoices.E: The loss of a family farm is often perceived as tragic even when no financial hardship results.

stimulus: Art critic: The aesthetic value of a work of art lies in its ability to impart a stimulating character to the audience's experience of the work.
questionStem: Which one of the following judgments most closely conforms with the principle cited above?

answerChoices.A: This painting is aesthetically deficient because it is an exact copy of a painting done 30 years ago.
answerChoices.B: This symphony is beautiful because, even though it does not excite the audience, it is competently performed.
answerChoices.C: This sculpted four-inch cube is beautiful because it is carved from material which, although much like marble, is very rare.
answerChoices.D: This painting is aesthetically valuable because it was painted by a highly controversial artist.
answerChoices.E: This poem is aesthetically deficient because it has little impact on its audience.

stimulus: Many of the presidents and prime ministers who have had the most successful foreign policies had no prior experience in foreign affairs when they assumed office. Although scholars and diplomats in the sacrosanct inner circle of international affairs would have us think otherwise, anyone with an acute political sense, a disciplined temperament, and a highly developed ability to absorb and retain information can quickly learn to conduct a successful foreign policy. In fact, prior experience alone will be of little value to a foreign policymaker who lacks all three of these traits.
questionStem: If all of the statements above are true, which one of the following must be true?

answerChoices.A: Scholars and diplomats have more experience in foreign affairs than most presidents and prime ministers bring to office.
answerChoices.B: Prior experience in foreign affairs is neither a sufficient nor a necessary condition for a president or prime minister to have a successful foreign policy.
answerChoices.C: Prior experience in foreign affairs is a necessary but not sufficient condition for a president or prime minister to have a successful foreign policy.
answerChoices.D: An acute political sense, a disciplined temperament, and a highly developed ability to absorb and retain information are each necessary conditions for a president or prime minister to have a successful foreign policy.
answerChoices.E: A president or prime minister with years of experience in foreign affairs will have a more successful foreign policy than one who does not have experience in foreign affairs.

stimulus: City council member: Despite the city's desperate need to exploit any available source of revenue, the mayor has repeatedly blocked council members' attempts to pass legislation imposing real estate development fees. It is clear that in doing so the mayor is sacrificing the city's interests to personal interests. The mayor cites figures to show that, in the current market, fees of the size proposed would significantly reduce the number of building starts and thus, on balance, result in a revenue loss to the city. But the important point is that the mayor's family is heavily involved in real estate development and thus has a strong financial interest in the matter.
questionStem: The reasoning in the city council member's argument is flawed because

answerChoices.A: the issue of the mayor's personal interest in the proposed legislation is irrelevant to any assessment of the mayor's action with respect to that legislation
answerChoices.B: the mayor's course of action being personally advantageous is not inconsistent with the mayor's action being advantageous for the city
answerChoices.C: the council member's own absence of personal interest in the proposed legislation has not been established
answerChoices.D: that a person or a municipality has a need for something does not, in itself, establish that that person or that municipality has a right to that thing
answerChoices.E: the possibility remains open that the mayor's need to avoid loss of family revenue is as desperate as the city's need to increase municipal revenue

stimulus: Until 1985 all commercial airlines completely replenished the cabin air in planes in flight once every 30 minutes. Since then the rate has been once every hour. The less frequently cabin air is replenished in a plane in flight, the higher the level of carbon dioxide in that plane and the easier it is for airborne illnesses to be spread.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

answerChoices.A: In 1985 there was a loosening of regulations concerning cabin air in commercial airline flights.
answerChoices.B: People who fly today are more likely to contract airborne illnesses than were people who flew prior to 1985.
answerChoices.C: Low levels of carbon dioxide in cabin air make it impossible for airborne illnesses to spread.
answerChoices.D: In 1980 the rate at which the cabin air was replenished in commercial airliners was sufficient to protect passengers from the effects of carbon dioxide buildup.
answerChoices.E: In 1980 the level of carbon dioxide in the cabin air on a two-hour commercial airline flight was lower than it is today on a similar flight.

stimulus: Doctors urge people to reduce their cholesterol levels through dietary changes. But moderate dietary changes often do not work to lower cholesterol levels. One may need, therefore, to make more dramatic changes, such as switching to a vegetarian diet.
questionStem: The statement that moderate dietary changes often do not work to lower cholesterol levels plays which one of the following roles in the argument?

answerChoices.A: It is presented to counter doctors’ suggestions that cholesterol levels can be reduced through dietary changes.
answerChoices.B: It is a premise offered in support of the claim that vegetarian diets are more healthful than any diets containing meat.
answerChoices.C: It is a premise offered in support of the claim that reducing cholesterol levels may require greater than moderate dietary changes.
answerChoices.D: It is offered as an explanation of the success of vegetarian diets in reducing cholesterol levels.
answerChoices.E: It is a conclusion for which the claim that dramatic changes in one’s diet are sometimes required to reduce cholesterol levels is offered as support.

stimulus: Artists have different ways of producing contours and hatching, and analysis of these stylistic features can help to distinguish works by a famous artist both from forgeries and from works genuinely by other artists. Indeed, this analysis has shown that many of the drawings formerly attributed to Michelangelo are actually by the artist Giulio Clovio, Michelangelo’s contemporary.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, then which one of the following must also be true?

answerChoices.A: Contours and hatching are the main features that distinguish the drawing styles of different artists.
answerChoices.B: Many of the drawings formerly attributed to Michelangelo are actually forgeries.
answerChoices.C: No forgery can perfectly duplicate the contour and hatching styles of a famous artist.
answerChoices.D: The contour and hatching styles used to identify the drawings of Clovio cited can be shown to be features of all Clovio’s works.
answerChoices.E: There is an analyzable difference between Clovio’s contour and hatching styles and those of Michelangelo.

stimulus: Advertisement: Each of the Economic Merit Prize winners from the past 25 years is covered by the Acme retirement plan. Since the winners of the nation’s most prestigious award for economists have thus clearly recognized that the Acme plan offers them a financially secure future, it is probably a good plan for anyone with retirement needs similar to theirs. The advertisement’s argumentation is most vulnerable to
questionStem: criticism on which one of the following grounds?

answerChoices.A: It ignores the possibility that the majority of Economic Merit Prize winners from previous years used a retirement plan other than the Acme plan.
answerChoices.B: It fails to address adequately the possibility that any of several retirement plans would be good enough for, and offer a financially secure future to, Economic Merit Prize winners.
answerChoices.C: It appeals to the fact that supposed experts have endorsed the argument’s main conclusion, rather than appealing to direct evidence for that conclusion.
answerChoices.D: It takes for granted that some winners of the Economic Merit Prize have deliberately selected the Acme retirement plan, rather than having had it chosen for them by their employers.
answerChoices.E: It presumes, without providing justification, that each of the Economic Merit Prize winners has retirement plan needs that are identical to the advertisement’s intended audience’s retirement plan needs.

stimulus: A small car offers less protection in an accident than a large car does, but since a smaller car is more maneuverable, it is better to drive a small car because then accidents will be less likely.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments employs reasoning most similar to that employed by the argument above?

answerChoices.A: An artist’s best work is generally that done in the time before the artist becomes very well known. When artists grow famous and are diverted from artistic creation by demands for public appearances, their artistic work suffers. So artists’ achieving great fame can diminish their artistic reputations.
answerChoices.B: It is best to insist that a child spend at least some time every day reading indoors. Even though it may cause the child some unhappiness to have to stay indoors when others are outside playing, the child can benefit from the time by learning to enjoy books and becoming prepared for lifelong learning.
answerChoices.C: For this work, vehicles built of lightweight materials are more practical than vehicles built of heavy materials. This is so because while lighter vehicles do not last as long as heavier vehicles, they are cheaper to replace.
answerChoices.D: Although it is important to limit the amount of sugar and fat in one’s diet, it would be a mistake to try to follow a diet totally lacking in sugar and fat. It is better to consume sugar and fat in moderation, for then the cravings that lead to uncontrolled binges will be prevented.
answerChoices.E: A person who exercises vigorously every day has less body fat than an average person to draw upon in the event of a wasting illness. But one should still endeavor to exercise vigorously every day, because doing so significantly decreases the chances of contracting a wasting illness.

stimulus:
Maria: Popular music is bad art because it greatly exaggerates the role love plays in everyday life and thereby fails to represent reality accurately.
Theo: Popular music is not supposed to reflect reality; it performs other artistic functions, such as providing consoling fantasies and helping people create some romance in their often difficult lives. You should understand popular music before you condemn it.
questionStem: The dialogue provides the most support for the claim that Maria and Theo disagree over whether

answerChoices.A: most good art creates consoling illusions
answerChoices.B: some bad art exaggerates the role love plays in everyday life
answerChoices.C: art should always represent reality as it could be, not as it is
answerChoices.D: art need not represent reality accurately to be good art
answerChoices.E: popular music should not be considered to be an art form

stimulus: The use of phrases like "as so-and-so said" or "as the saying goes" suggests that the quote that follows has just been illustrated. Such phrases are inappropriately used when an apparent counterexample has just been given.
questionStem: Which one of the following contains an inappropriate usage of a phrase, according to the principle stated above?

answerChoices.A: Fatima was a mathematician who often thought about unsolved problems of mathematics, although it was unpleasant to be reminded that most would probably remain unsolved in her lifetime. As the saying goes, "Strange how much you've got to know before you know how little you know."
answerChoices.B: Harold's friends were surprised when he revealed that he had left his wallet at home and asked that someone lend him money. But he had done the same thing many times before. As Halliard said, "The force of selfishness is as inevitable and as calculable as the force of gravitation."
answerChoices.C: The best model of vacuum cleaner was the most expensive on the market, but it would have made Roger unhappy to purchase it. For although he never wanted anything but the best, he was also quite frugal, and would never have forgiven himself for spending the money. As the saying goes, "A penny saved is a penny earned."
answerChoices.D: Sharon loved cats, but her husband was allergic to them. Still, he was occasionally willing to accompany her to cat shows. As the saying goes, "Shared lives mean shared loves."
answerChoices.E: Raoul spent a year planning and preparing for a fantastic ski trip. He enjoyed his ski trip greatly until he broke his leg and had to spend two weeks in the hospital. As the saying goes, "All's well that ends well."

stimulus: In criminal proceedings, defense attorneys occasionally attempt to establish that a suspect was not present at the commission of a crime by comparing the suspect's DNA to the DNA of blood or hair samples taken from the scene of the crime. Although every person's DNA is unique, DNA tests often fail to distinguish among DNA samples taken from distinct individuals. Hence, it is a mistake to exonerate a suspect simply because that person's DNA did not match the DNA samples taken from the scene of the crime.
questionStem: Which one of the following is an error in the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: It assumes without warrant that the use of physical evidence in identifying suspects is never mistaken.
answerChoices.B: It confuses a test that incorrectly identifies DNA samples as coming from the same person with a test that incorrectly shows as coming from different persons samples that come from a single person.
answerChoices.C: It generalizes about the reliability of all methods used to identify those involved in the commission of a crime on the basis of results that pertain to only a few such methods.
answerChoices.D: It relies on experimental data derived from DNA testing that have not been shown to hold under nonexperimental conditions.
answerChoices.E: It fails to demonstrate that physical evidence taken from the scene of a crime is the only sort of evidence that should be admitted in criminal court proceedings.

stimulus: Psychiatrist: Take any visceral emotion you care to consider. There are always situations in which it is healthy to try to express that emotion. So, there are always situations in which it is healthy to try to express one’s anger.
questionStem: The conclusion of the argument follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Anger is always expressible.
answerChoices.B: Anger is a visceral emotion.
answerChoices.C: Some kinds of emotions are unhealthy to express.
answerChoices.D: All emotions that are healthy to express are visceral.
answerChoices.E: An emotion is visceral only if it is healthy to express.

stimulus: Cigarette companies claim that manufacturing both low- and high-nicotine cigarettes allows smokers to choose how much nicotine they want. However, a recent study has shown that the levels of nicotine found in the blood of smokers who smoke one pack of cigarettes per day are identical at the end of a day’s worth of smoking, whatever the level of nicotine in the cigarettes they smoke.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the finding of the nicotine study?

answerChoices.A: Blood cannot absorb more nicotine per day than that found in the smoke from a package of the lowest-nicotine cigarettes available.
answerChoices.B: Smokers of the lowest-nicotine cigarettes available generally smoke more cigarettes per day than smokers of high-nicotine cigarettes.
answerChoices.C: Most nicotine is absorbed into the blood of a smoker even if it is delivered in smaller quantities.
answerChoices.D: The level of tar in cigarettes is higher in low- nicotine cigarettes than it is in some high- nicotine cigarettes.
answerChoices.E: When taking in nicotine by smoking cigarettes is discontinued, the level of nicotine in the blood decreases steadily.

stimulus: Biologist: Humans have five fingers because we descended from a fish with five phalanges in its fins. Despite our prejudices to the contrary, our configuration of fingers is no more or less useful than several other possible configurations, e.g., six per hand. So, if humans had descended from a fish with six phalanges in its fins and had six fingers on each hand, then we would be just as content with that configuration.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the biologist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Everyone is equally content with our present configuration of fingers.
answerChoices.B: Humans are never equally content with two things of unequal usefulness.
answerChoices.C: Humans are always equally content with two things of equal usefulness.
answerChoices.D: The perceived usefulness of our configuration of fingers is an illusory result of our prejudices.
answerChoices.E: At least one species of fish had six phalanges in its fins.

stimulus: Some vegetarians have argued that there are two individually sufficient reasons for not eating meat—one based on health considerations, and the other based on the aversion to living at the expense of other conscious creatures. But suppose that eating meat were essential to good health for humans. Then it would be less clear that an aversion to living at the expense of other conscious creatures is enough of a reason to stop eating meat.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes the role played in the argument by the supposition that eating meat is essential to good health?

answerChoices.A: It is used to disprove the vegetarian position that we should not eat meat.
answerChoices.B: It is used to show that the two types of reasons cited in favor of vegetarianism are independent.
answerChoices.C: It is used to disprove the claim that a vegetarian diet is healthy.
answerChoices.D: It is used to weaken the claim that the consciousness of animals is a sufficient reason for not eating meat.
answerChoices.E: It is used to show that there is no sufficient reason for not eating meat.

stimulus: Decentralization enables divisions of a large institution to function autonomously. This always permits more realistic planning and strongly encourages innovation, since the people responsible for decision making are directly involved in implementing the policies they design. Decentralization also permits the central administration to focus on institution-wide issues without being overwhelmed by the details of daily operations.
questionStem: The statements above most strongly support which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: In large institutions whose divisions do not function autonomously, planning is not maximally realistic.
answerChoices.B: Innovation is not always encouraged in large centralized institutions.
answerChoices.C: For large institutions the advantages of decentralization outweigh its disadvantages.
answerChoices.D: The central administrations of large institutions are usually partially responsible for most of the details of daily operations.
answerChoices.E: The people directly involved in implementing policies are always able to make innovative and realistic policy decisions.

stimulus: Polling data reveal that an overwhelming majority of nine-year-olds can correctly identify the logos of major cigarette brands. However, of those nine-year-olds who recognize such logos, less than 1 percent smoke. Therefore, there is little or no connection between recognition of cigarette brand logos and smoking.
questionStem: Which one of the following uses flawed reasoning most similar to the flawed reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: The concern about the long-term effect on dolphins of small quantities of mercury in the ocean is unfounded. During a three-month observation period, 1,000 dolphins were exposed to small quantities of mercury in seawater, with no effect on the animals.
answerChoices.B: Many ten-year-olds dream of becoming actors. Yet it is not likely they will seriously consider becoming actors, because most parents discourage their children from pursuing such a highly competitive career.
answerChoices.C: Most dentists recommend using fluoride to reduce the incidence of cavities, but few recommend giving up candy entirely; so, using fluoride is probably more effective in preventing cavities than is avoiding sweets.
answerChoices.D: A large percentage of men exercise moderately throughout their lives, but the average life span of those who do so is not significantly greater than of those who get little or no exercise. So there is little or no correlation between moderate exercise and good health.
