answerChoices.E: Most people cannot name their legislative representatives. Nonetheless, this is insignificant, for when queried, most of them displayed an adequate command of current political issues.

stimulus: Sarah: Our regulations for staff review are vague and thus difficult to interpret. For instance, the regulations state that a staff member who is performing unsatisfactorily will face dismissal, but they fail to define unsatisfactory performance. Thus, some staff may be dismissed merely because their personal views conflict with those of their supervisors.
questionStem: Which one of the following generalizations, if applicable to Sarah's company, most helps to justify her reasoning?

answerChoices.A: Performance that falls only somewhat below expectations results in disciplinary measures short of dismissal.
answerChoices.B: Interpreting regulations is a prerogative that belongs solely to supervisors.
answerChoices.C: A vague regulation can be used to make those subject to it answer for their performance.
answerChoices.D: A vague regulation can be used to keep those subject to it in subordinate positions.
answerChoices.E: Employees usually consider specific regulations to be fairer than vague regulations.

stimulus: Chapin: Commentators have noted with concern the recent electoral success by extremist parties in several democratic countries. But these successes pose no threat to democracy in those countries. The extremists have won pluralities, not majorities. Furthermore, they have won only when the moderate parties were preoccupied with arguing among themselves.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if assumed, enables Chapin's conclusion to be properly drawn?

answerChoices.A: Parties that win pluralities but not majorities never directly or indirectly effect changes in their country's political arrangements.
answerChoices.B: Multiparty political systems are always more democratic than two-party political systems are.
answerChoices.C: Countries in which extremist parties win pluralities sometimes have democratic governments as strong as those in countries that lack extremist parties.
answerChoices.D: Members of moderate parties who consider extremist parties to be a serious threat to democracy will sometimes put aside their differences with each other to oppose them.
answerChoices.E: People are not always supporting a move toward an extremist government when they vote for extremist parties in democratic elections.

stimulus: University budget committee: Athletes experience fewer injuries on artificial-turf athletic fields than on natural-grass fields. Additionally, natural-grass fields are more expensive to maintain than fields made of artificial turf. Nevertheless, this committee recommends replacing the university's current artificial-turf field with a natural-grass field.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the committee's position?

answerChoices.A: The university's current artificial-turf athletic field has required extensive maintenance since its original installation.
answerChoices.B: Most injuries sustained on artificial-turf fields take longer to heal and require more expensive physical therapy than do injuries sustained on natural-grass fields.
answerChoices.C: It is difficult for spectators at athletic events to determine whether an athletic field is artificial turf or natural grass.
answerChoices.D: Maintaining artificial-turf fields involves the occasional replacement of damaged sections of turf, whereas natural-grass fields require daily watering and periodic fertilization.
answerChoices.E: Athletes who have spent most of their playing time on natural-grass fields generally prefer not to play on artificial-turf fields.

stimulus: Conscientiousness is high on most firms' list of traits they want in employees. Yet a recent study found that laid-off conscientious individuals are less likely to find jobs within five months than are their peers who shirked their workplace responsibilities.
questionStem: Each of the following, if true, helps to resolve the apparent paradox above except:

answerChoices.A: People who shirk their workplace responsibilities are less likely to keep the jobs they have, so there are more of them looking for jobs.
answerChoices.B: Conscientious people tend to have a greater than average concern with finding the job most suited to their interests and abilities.
answerChoices.C: Resentment about having been laid off in spite of their conscientiousness leads some people to perform poorly in interviews.
answerChoices.D: People who are inclined to shirk their workplace responsibilities are more likely to exaggerate their credentials, leading prospective employers to believe them to be highly qualified.
answerChoices.E: Finding a job is less urgent for the conscientious, because they tend to have larger savings.

stimulus: A safety report indicates that, on average, traffic fatalities decline by about 7 percent in those areas in which strict laws requiring drivers and passengers to wear seat belts have been passed. In a certain city, seat belt laws have been in effect for two years, but the city's public safety records show that the number of traffic deaths per year has remained the same.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, does not help resolve the apparent discrepancy between the safety report and the city's public safety records?

answerChoices.A: Two years ago speed limits in the city were increased by as much as 15 kph (9 mph).
answerChoices.B: The city now includes pedestrian fatalities in its yearly total of traffic deaths, whereas two years ago it did not.
answerChoices.C: In the time since the seat belt laws were passed, the city has experienced a higher than average increase in automobile traffic.
answerChoices.D: Because the city's seat belt laws have been so rarely enforced, few drivers in the city have complied with them.
answerChoices.E: In the last two years, most of the people killed in car accidents in the city were not wearing seat belts.

stimulus: Physician: Hatha yoga is a powerful tool for helping people quit smoking. In a clinical trial, those who practiced hatha yoga for 75 minutes once a week and received individual counseling reduced their smoking and cravings for tobacco as much as did those who went to traditional self-help groups once a week and had individual counseling.
questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the physician's argument relies?

answerChoices.A: The individual counseling received by the smokers in the clinical trial who practiced hatha yoga did not help them quit smoking.
answerChoices.B: Most smokers are able to practice hatha yoga more than once a week.
answerChoices.C: Traditional self-help groups are powerful tools for helping people quit smoking.
answerChoices.D: People who practice hatha yoga for 75 minutes once a week are not damaging themselves physically.
answerChoices.E: Other forms of yoga are less effective than hatha yoga in helping people quit smoking.

stimulus: Whoever is kind is loved by somebody or other, and whoever loves anyone is happy. It follows that whoever is kind is happy.
questionStem: The conclusion follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Whoever loves someone loves everyone.
answerChoices.B: Whoever loves everyone loves someone.
answerChoices.C: Whoever is happy loves everyone.
answerChoices.D: Whoever loves no one is loved by no one.
answerChoices.E: Whoever loves everyone is kind.

stimulus:
Moralist: TV talk shows are contributing to the moral decline in our country. By constantly being shown the least moral people in our society, viewers begin to think that such people are the norm, and that there is something wrong with being morally upright.
TV talk show host: Well, if there is such a decline, it's not because of TV talk shows: we simply show people what they want to see. What can be wrong with letting the viewers decide? Furthermore, if restrictions were put on my show, that would amount to censorship, which is wrong.
questionStem: The moralist's and the TV talk show host's statements provide the most support for holding that they disagree about whether

answerChoices.A: TV talk shows should be censored
answerChoices.B: people's moral standards have changed
answerChoices.C: TV talk shows influence people's conception of what is the norm
answerChoices.D: TV talk shows, by presenting immoral guests, are causing a moral decline
answerChoices.E: it is wrong not to let the viewers decide what they want to see

stimulus: For the last three years, entomologists have been searching for a parasite to help control a whitefly that has recently become a serious crop pest. Believing this new pest to be a variety of sweet-potato whitefly, the entomologists confined their search to parasites of the sweet-potato whitefly. Genetic research now shows the new pest to be a distinct species, the silverleaf whitefly. Therefore, the search for a parasite has so far been wasted effort.
questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument relies?

answerChoices.A: All varieties of the sweet-potato whitefly are serious crop pests.
answerChoices.B: If a crop pest has a parasite, that parasite can always be used to control that pest.
answerChoices.C: The chances of successfully identifying a useful parasite of the new pest have increased since the proper identification of the pest.
answerChoices.D: No parasite of the sweet-potato whitefly is also a parasite of the silverleaf whitefly.
answerChoices.E: In the last three years, the entomologists found no parasites of the sweet-potato whitefly.

stimulus: Social critic: The whole debate over the legal right of rock singers to utter violent lyrics misses the point. Legally, there is very little that may not be said. But not everything that may legally be said, ought to be said. Granted, violence predates the rise in popularity of such music. Yet words also have the power to change the way we see and the way we act.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the passage?

answerChoices.A: If rock music that contains violent lyrics is morally wrong, then it should be illegal.
answerChoices.B: The law should be changed so that the government is mandated to censor rock music that contains violent lyrics.
answerChoices.C: Violent rock song lyrics do not incite violence, they merely reflect the violence in society.
answerChoices.D: If rock musicians voluntarily censor their violent lyrics, this may help to reduce violence in society.
answerChoices.E: Stopping the production of rock music that contains violent lyrics would eliminate much of the violence within society.

stimulus: Editorial: When legislators discover that some public service is not being adequately provided, their most common response is to boost the funding for that public service. Because of this, the least efficiently run government bureaucracies are the ones that most commonly receive an increase in funds.
questionStem: The statements in the editorial, if true, most strongly support which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: The least efficiently run government bureaucracies are the bureaucracies that legislators most commonly discover to be failing to provide some public service adequately.
answerChoices.B: When legislators discover that a public service is not being adequately provided, they never respond to the problem by reducing the funding of the government bureaucracy providing that service.
answerChoices.C: Throughout the time a government bureaucracy is run inefficiently, legislators repeatedly boost the funding for the public service that this bureaucracy provides.
answerChoices.D: If legislators boost funding for a public service, the government bureaucracy providing that service will commonly become less efficient as a result.
answerChoices.E: The most inefficiently run government bureaucracy receives the most funding of any government bureaucracy.

stimulus: Fred argued that, since Kathleen is a successful film director, she has probably worked with famous actors. But, while Fred is right in supposing that most successful film directors work with famous actors, his conclusion is not warranted. For, as he knows, Kathleen works only on documentary films, and directors of documentaries rarely work with famous actors.
questionStem: Which one of the following strategies is used above to criticize Fred's reasoning?

answerChoices.A: maintaining that too little is known about Kathleen to justify any conclusion
answerChoices.B: showing that Kathleen must not have worked with famous actors
answerChoices.C: claiming that Fred has failed to take relevant information into account
answerChoices.D: showing that Fred has mistakenly assumed that all successful film directors work with famous actors
answerChoices.E: demonstrating that Fred has failed to show that most successful film directors work with famous actors

stimulus: It is characteristic of great artists generally, and of great writers in particular, to have a discerning view of the basic social and political arrangements of the society in which they live. Therefore, the greater a writer one is, the more astute one will be in perceiving the basic social and political arrangements of one's society.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes a flaw in the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: It assumes, without providing justification, that members of a group that is part of a larger group possess all of the characteristics possessed by members of the larger group.
answerChoices.B: It assumes, without providing justification, that because something is sometimes the case it must always be the case.
answerChoices.C: It assumes, without providing justification, that those artists with political insight do not have insight into matters outside of politics.
answerChoices.D: It assumes, without providing justification, that only great individuals can make discerning criticisms of their societies.
answerChoices.E: It assumes, without providing justification, that because people who have one quality tend to have a second quality, those who have more of the first quality will have more of the second.

stimulus: Psychologist: Some people contend that children should never be reprimanded. Any criticism, let alone punishment, they say, harms children's self-esteem. This view is laudable in its challenge to the belief that children should be punished whenever they misbehave, yet it gives a dangerous answer to the question of how often punishment should be inflicted. When parents never reprimand their children, they are in effect rewarding them for unacceptable behavior, and rewarded behavior tends to recur.
questionStem: The view that children should never be reprimanded functions in the psychologist's argument as a statement of a position that the psychologist's argument

answerChoices.A: is designed to discredit entirely
answerChoices.B: is designed to establish as true
answerChoices.C: is designed to establish as well intentioned
answerChoices.D: claims has a serious flaw though is not without value
answerChoices.E: claims is less reasonable than any other view mentioned

stimulus: Town councillor: The only reason for the town to have ordinances restricting where skateboarding can be done would be to protect children from danger. Skateboarding in the town's River Park is undoubtedly dangerous, but we should not pass an ordinance prohibiting it. If children cannot skateboard in the park, they will most certainly skateboard in the streets. And skateboarding in the streets is more dangerous than skateboarding in the park.
questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if established, would provide the strongest support for the town councillor's argument?

answerChoices.A: Ordinances that restrict the recreational activities of a town's inhabitants should not be passed unless those activities pose a danger to participants.
answerChoices.B: Since the town could be legally liable for accidents that occur on public property, town ordinances should restrict any unnecessarily dangerous activities in publicly owned areas.
answerChoices.C: Since safety in a recreational activity depends on the level of skill of the participant in that activity, the regulation of children's recreational activities should be left to the discretion of the children's parents.
answerChoices.D: If recreational activities constitute a danger to the participants in those activities, then the town council should enact ordinances prohibiting those activities.
answerChoices.E: Ordinances that seek to eliminate dangers should not be enacted if their enactment would lead to dangers that are greater than those they seek to eliminate.

stimulus: Considering that Mark Twain is Samuel Clemens, I have always found it amazing that very few people know that Samuel Clemens was a writer, since almost everybody knows that Mark Twain was one.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would most effectively resolve the apparent paradox above?

answerChoices.A: Most people probably have not read anything by Samuel Clemens.
answerChoices.B: Everyone who knows that Samuel Clemens was a writer also knows that Mark Twain was one.
answerChoices.C: Most people do not know that Mark Twain is Samuel Clemens.
answerChoices.D: Many people believe apparently conflicting things about authors.
answerChoices.E: Some people know that "Mark Twain" is a pseudonym for Samuel Clemens.

stimulus:
James: Many people claim that the voting public is unable to evaluate complex campaign issues. The television commercials for Reade in the national campaign, however, discuss complex campaign issues, and Reade is, at present, more popular than any other candidate.
Maria: Yes, Reade is the most popular. However, you are incorrect in claiming that this is because of Reade's discussion of complex campaign issues. Reade simply strikes the voters as the most competent and trustworthy candidate.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most supports Maria's counter to James?

answerChoices.A: Reade's opponents are discussing some of the same issues as Reade.
answerChoices.B: Reade's opponents charge that Reade oversimplifies complex campaign issues.
answerChoices.C: Polling data show that Reade's present popularity will probably diminish over time.
answerChoices.D: Polling data show that most voters cannot identify Reade's positions on campaign issues.
answerChoices.E: Polling data show that some voters consider Reade competent and trustworthy.

stimulus:
Marta: There have been complaints about the lack of recreational areas in our city. Some people favor turning the old railway land into walking trails, but there may be more productive ways of using that land.
Arthur: But the old railway land is ideal for walking trails. Our citizens have gone too long with inadequate recreational areas; we should not dismiss this proposal for walking trails without further consideration.
questionStem: Arthur's criticism suggests that he interpreted Marta to be

answerChoices.A: maintaining that converting the old railway land into walking trails would be an entirely unproductive use of that land
answerChoices.B: favoring the development of recreational areas other than walking trails
answerChoices.C: assuming that the complaints concerning a shortage of recreational areas are ill founded
answerChoices.D: recommending that the proposal for converting the old railway land into walking trails should be promptly dismissed
answerChoices.E: asserting that it may not be possible to convert the old railway land into adequate walking trails

stimulus: Recent investigations of earthquakes have turned up a previously unknown type of seismic shock, known as a displacement pulse, which is believed to be present in all earthquakes. Alarmingly, high-rise buildings are especially vulnerable to displacement pulses, according to computer models. Yet examination of high-rises within cities damaged by recent powerful earthquakes indicates little significant damage to these structures.
questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, contributes to a
resolution of the apparent paradox?

answerChoices.A: Displacement pulses travel longer distances than other types of seismic shock.
answerChoices.B: Scientific predictions based on computer models often fail when tested in the field.
answerChoices.C: While displacement pulses have only recently been discovered, they have accompanied all earthquakes that have ever occurred.
answerChoices.D: The displacement pulses made by low-and medium-intensity earthquakes are much less powerful than those made by the strongest earthquakes.
answerChoices.E: Computer models have been very successful in predicting the effects of other types of seismic shock.

stimulus: Film historians have made two major criticisms of Depression-era filmmakers: first, that they were too uncritical of the economic status quo; and second, that they self-indulgently created films reflecting their own dreams and desires. However, these filmmakers made their movies with an eye to profit, and so they provided what their audiences most wanted in a film: a chance to imagine being wealthy enough not to have a care in the world. Thus, the second criticism cannot be accurate.
questionStem: The conclusion of the argument follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: To avoid self-indulgence, filmmakers should take a critical stance toward the existing economic system and should allow audiences to form their own personal aspirations.
answerChoices.B: It is unjustified to demand of all filmmakers that their films engage in criticism of the economic status quo.
answerChoices.C: The people who regularly went to movies during the Depression were those likely to have been most satisfied with the economic status quo.
answerChoices.D: Depression-era filmmakers who did not make films for profit could not take radical critical stances toward then-current economic and political issues.
answerChoices.E: It cannot be self-indulgent for a filmmaker to give an audience what it most wants.

stimulus: Often, a product popularly believed to be the best of its type is no better than any other; rather, the product’s reputation, which may be independent of its quality, provides its owner with status. Thus, although there is no harm in paying for status if that is what one wants, one should know that one is paying for prestige, not quality.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

answerChoices.A: Often, choosing the best job offer is a matter of comparing the undesirable features of the different jobs. Thus, those who choose a job because it has a desirable location should know that they might be unhappy with its hours.
answerChoices.B: Most people have little tolerance for boastfulness. Thus, although one’s friends may react positively when hearing the details of one’s accomplishments, it is unlikely that their reactions are entirely honest.
answerChoices.C: Those beginning a new hobby sometimes quit it because of the frustrations involved in learning a new skill. Thus, although it is fine to try to learn a skill quickly, one is more likely to learn a skill if one first learns to enjoy the process of acquiring it.
answerChoices.D: Personal charm is often confused with virtue. Thus, while there is nothing wrong with befriending a charming person, anyone who does so should realize that a charming friend is not necessarily a good and loyal friend.
answerChoices.E: Many theatrical actors cannot enjoy watching a play because when they watch others, they yearn to be on stage themselves. Thus, although there is no harm in yearning to perform, such performers should, for their own sakes, learn to suppress that yearning.

stimulus: There have been no new cases of naturally occurring polio in North America in recent years. Yet there are approximately 12 new cases of polio each year in North America, all caused by the commonly administered live oral polio vaccine (OPV). Substituting inactivated polio vaccine (IPV) for most childhood polio immunizations would cut the number of cases of vaccination-caused polio about in half. Clearly it is time to switch from OPV to IPV as the most commonly used polio vaccine for North American children.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

answerChoices.A: If IPV replaces OPV as the most commonly used polio vaccine, at least a few new cases of naturally occurring polio in North America will result each year.
answerChoices.B: The vast majority of cases of polio caused by OPV have occurred in children with preexisting but unsuspected immunodeficiency disorders.
answerChoices.C: A child’s risk of contracting polio from OPV has been estimated at 1 in 8.7 million, which is significantly less than the risk of being struck by lightning.
answerChoices.D: Although IPV is preferred in some European nations, most countries with comprehensive child immunization programs use OPV.
answerChoices.E: IPV, like most vaccines, carries a slight risk of inducing seizures in children with neurological diseases such as epilepsy.

stimulus:
Columnist: There are certain pesticides that, even though they have been banned for use in the United States for nearly 30 years, are still manufactured there and exported to other countries. In addition
to jeopardizing the health of people in these other countries, this practice greatly increases the health risk to U.S. consumers, for these pesticides are often used on agricultural products imported into the United States.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the columnist’s argument?

answerChoices.A: Trace amounts of some of the pesticides banned for use in the United States can be detected in the soil where they were used 30 years ago.
answerChoices.B: Most of the pesticides that are manufactured in the United States and exported are not among those banned for use in the United States.
answerChoices.C: The United States is not the only country that manufactures and exports the pesticides that are banned for use in the United States.
answerChoices.D: The banned pesticides pose a greater risk to people in the countries in which they are used than to U.S. consumers.
answerChoices.E: There are many pesticides that are banned for use in other countries that are not banned for use in the United States.

stimulus: Being near woodlands, the natural habitat of bees, promotes the health of crops that depend on pollination. Bees, the most common pollinators, visit flowers far from woodlands less often than they visit flowers close to woodlands.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

answerChoices.A: The likelihood that a plant is pollinated increases as the number of visits from pollinators increases.
answerChoices.B: Many bees live in habitats other than woodlands.
answerChoices.C: Woodlands are not the natural habitat of all pollinators.
answerChoices.D: Some pollinators visit flowers far from their habitats more often than they visit flowers close to their habitats.
answerChoices.E: Many crops that are not near woodlands depend on pollination.

stimulus: According to the rules of the university’s housing lottery, the only students guaranteed dormitory rooms are fourthyear students. In addition, any fourth-year student on the dean’s list can choose a dormitory room before anyone who is not a fourth-year student.
questionStem: Which one of the following inferences is most strongly supported by the rules described above?

answerChoices.A: Benizer is a fourth-year student who is not on the dean’s list, so she is not guaranteed a dormitory room.
answerChoices.B: Ivan and Naomi are both fourth-year students but only Naomi is on the dean’s list. Therefore, Ivan can choose a dormitory room before Naomi.
answerChoices.C: Halle, a third-year student, is on the dean’s list. Thus, she is guaranteed a dormitory room.
answerChoices.D: Gerald and Katrina are both on the dean’s list but only Gerald is a fourth-year student. Thus, Gerald can choose a dormitory room before Katrina.
answerChoices.E: Anissa is a fourth-year student who is on the dean’s list. Thus, since Jehan is a second-year student who is also on the dean’s list, he can choose a dormitory room before Anissa.

stimulus:
To the editor:
For generations, magnificent racehorses have been bred in our area. Our most valuable product, however, has been generations of children raised with the character that makes them winners in the contests of life. Gambling is wrong, and children raised in an atmosphere where the goal is to get something for nothing will not develop good character. Those who favor developing good character in children over gambling on horses should vote against allowing our first racetrack to be built.
L.E.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens L.E.’s argument?

answerChoices.A: If good character is developed in children early, the children continue to have good character in different environments.
answerChoices.B: In other areas with gambling, parents are able to raise children of good character.
answerChoices.C: In most areas with horse racing, the percentage of adults who gamble increases gradually from year to year.
answerChoices.D: Children whose parents gamble do not necessarily gamble when they become adults.
answerChoices.E: Where voters have had the opportunity to vote on horse racing, they have consistently approved it.

stimulus: Overexposure to certain wavelengths of strong sunlight is the main cause of melanoma, a virulent form of skin cancer. For this reason, doctors now urge everyone to put adequate sunblock on skin exposed to strong sunlight. Adequate sunblock, according to doctors, is any preparation that prevents sunburn even if the person is exposed to strong sunlight for a significant length of time.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the recommendation that people wear adequate sunblock?

answerChoices.A: There is no evidence that there are wavelengths of sunlight that lead to both sunburn and melanoma.
answerChoices.B: There are people who have allergic reactions to certain chemicals found in many sunblocks.
answerChoices.C: Many sunblocks need repeated applications to remain effective for a significant length of time.
answerChoices.D: Toxins contained in certain chemical compounds also cause melanoma.
answerChoices.E: Sunburns appear immediately after exposure to the sun but melanoma appears years after repeated exposures.

stimulus: Philosopher: It is absurd to argue that people are morally obligated to act in a certain way simply because not acting in that way would be unnatural. An unnatural action is either a violation of the laws of nature or a statistical anomaly. There is no possibility of acting as one cannot, nor does the mere fact that something is not usually done provide any good reason not to do it.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes a technique used in the philosopher’s argument?

answerChoices.A: undermining a concept by showing that its acceptance would violate a law of nature
answerChoices.B: stating the definition of a key term of the argument
answerChoices.C: using statistical findings to dispute a claim
answerChoices.D: undermining a claim by showing that the claim is self-contradictory
answerChoices.E: using empirical evidence to support one definition of a key term of the argument over another

stimulus: It has been a staple of drama to feature an innocent young protagonist, eager to make a mark on the world, who is stymied by an indifferent or hostile society. Since the playwrights of such works wished the audience to empathize with the protagonist, historians do not regard these plays as serious revelations of what the societies presented in the plays were really like.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the viewpoint of the historians described above?

answerChoices.A: The historians believe that playwrights tend to be more critical of their own societies than of other societies.
answerChoices.B: The historians believe that playwrights tend to exaggerate the weaknesses of a society for the sake of dramatic effect.
answerChoices.C: The historians believe that plays tend to provide useful information about the time and society in which they were written.
answerChoices.D: The historians believe that plays often contain serious revelations of what the societies presented in those plays were like.
answerChoices.E: The historians believe that only the most popular plays within a society accurately portray that society.

stimulus: A television manufacturing plant has a total of 1,000 workers, though an average of 10 are absent on any given day for various reasons. On days when exactly 10 workers are absent, the plant produces televisions at its normal rate. Thus, it is reasonable to assume that the plant could fire 10 workers without any loss in production.
questionStem: The argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it

answerChoices.A: ignores the possibility that if 10 workers were fired, each of the remaining workers would produce more televisions than previously
answerChoices.B: fails to show that the absentee rate would drop if 10 workers were fired
answerChoices.C: takes for granted that the normal rate of production can be attained only when no more than the average number of workers are absent
answerChoices.D: overlooks the possibility that certain workers are crucial to the production of televisions
answerChoices.E: takes for granted that the rate of production is not affected by the number of workers employed at the plant

stimulus: Extinction is inevitable for all biological species. In fact, the vast majority of all species that have ever lived are now extinct. Since all species die out eventually, there is no justification for trying to protect species that are presently endangered, even those that can be saved from extinction now.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most closely paralleled by the argument that there is no reason to

answerChoices.A: look for a book in the library because it is sometimes checked out
answerChoices.B: spend money on preventive maintenance of a car because no car can last indefinitely
answerChoices.C: reinforce bridges against earthquakes in earthquake-prone areas because earthquakes occur only very infrequently
answerChoices.D: take a route that will avoid the normal traffic jams because traffic jams can occur along any route
answerChoices.E: plant a flower garden in soil that is not beneficial to plants because the plants are likely to die in such soil

stimulus: Most business ethics courses and textbooks confine themselves to considering specific cases and principles. For example, students are often given lists of ethical rules for in-class discussion and role-playing. This approach fails to provide a framework for understanding specific principles and should thus be changed to include abstract ethical theory.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if valid, most helps to justify the reasoning above?

answerChoices.A: A moralizing approach that fails to recognize the diversity of the ethical rules in use is unacceptable.
answerChoices.B: Courses that concentrate mainly on role-playing are undesirable because students must adopt alien personae.
answerChoices.C: People have no obligation to always behave ethically unless they are acquainted with abstract ethical theory.
answerChoices.D: Abstract ethical theory is the most appropriate of any context for understanding specific principles.
answerChoices.E: An ethics course should acquaint students with a wide range of specific principles and appropriate applications.

stimulus: Analyst: A recent survey showed that although professors of biology who teach but do not pursue research made up one twentieth of all science professors, they were appointed to fewer than one twentieth of all the scientific administrative positions in universities. We can conclude from this survey that failing to pursue research tends to bias university administrators against appointing these professors to scientific administrative positions.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the support for the analyst's conclusion?

answerChoices.A: In universities there are fewer scientific administrative positions than there are nonscientific administrative positions.
answerChoices.B: Biologists who do research fill a disproportionately low number of scientific administrative positions in universities.
answerChoices.C: Biology professors get more than one twentieth of all the science grant money available.
answerChoices.D: Conducting biological research tends to take significantly more time than does teaching biology.
answerChoices.E: Biologists who hold scientific administrative positions in the university tend to hold those positions for a shorter time than do other science professors.

stimulus: Catmull: Although historians consider themselves to be social scientists, different historians never arrive at the same conclusions about specific events of the past. Thus historians never determine what actually happened; like novelists, they merely create interesting fictional stories about the many different problems that people have faced.
questionStem: The reasoning in Catmull's argument is flawed because the argument

answerChoices.A: draws a conclusion that simply restates a claim presented in support of that conclusion
answerChoices.B: concludes, solely on the basis of the claim that different people have reached different conclusions about a topic, that none of these conclusions is true
answerChoices.C: presumes, without providing justification, that unless historians' conclusions are objectively true, they have no value whatsoever
answerChoices.D: bases its conclusion on premises that contradict each other
answerChoices.E: mistakes a necessary condition for the objective truth of historians' conclusions for a sufficient condition for the objective truth of those conclusions

stimulus: In a poll conducted by interviewing eligible voters in their homes just before the recent election, incumbent candidate Kenner was significantly ahead of candidate Muratori. Nonetheless, Muratori won the recent election.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy described by the statements above?

answerChoices.A: The positions taken by Muratori and Kenner on many election issues were not very similar to each other.
answerChoices.B: Kenner had held elected office for many years before the recent election.
answerChoices.C: In the year leading up to the election, Kenner was implicated in a series of political scandals.
answerChoices.D: Six months before the recent election, the voting age was lowered by three years.
answerChoices.E: In the poll, supporters of Muratori were more likely than others to describe the election as important.

stimulus: Reza: Language requires the use of verbal signs for objects as well as for feelings. Many animals can vocally express hunger, but only humans can ask for an egg or an apple by naming it. And using verbal signs for objects requires the ability to distinguish these objects from other objects, which in turn requires conceptual thought.
questionStem: If all of Reza's statements are true, then which one of the following must also be true?

answerChoices.A: Conceptual thought is required for language.
answerChoices.B: Conceptual thought requires the use of verbal signs for objects.
answerChoices.C: It is not possible to think conceptually about feelings.
answerChoices.D: All humans are capable of conceptual thought.
answerChoices.E: The vocal expressions of animals other than humans do not require conceptual thought.

stimulus: The best explanation for Mozart's death involves the recently detected fracture in his skull. The crack, most likely the result of an accident, could have easily torn veins in his brain, allowing blood to leak into his brain. When such bleeding occurs in the brain and the blood dries, many of the brain's faculties become damaged, commonly, though not immediately, leading to death. This explanation of Mozart's death is bolstered by the fact that the fracture shows signs of partial healing.
questionStem: The claim that the fracture shows signs of partial healing figures in the argument in which one of the following ways?

answerChoices.A: It shows that Mozart's death could have been avoided.
answerChoices.B: It shows that the fracture did not occur after Mozart's death.
answerChoices.C: It shows that the dried blood impaired Mozart's brain's faculties.
answerChoices.D: It shows that Mozart's death occurred suddenly.
answerChoices.E: It suggests that Mozart's death was accidental.

stimulus: This stamp is probably highly valuable, since it exhibits a printing error. The most important factors in determining a stamp's value, assuming it is in good condition, are its rarity and age. This is clearly a fine specimen, and it is quite old as well.
questionStem: The conclusion is properly inferred if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: The older a stamp is, the more valuable it is.
answerChoices.B: Printing errors are always confined to a few individual stamps.
answerChoices.C: Most stamps with printing errors are already in the hands of collectors.
answerChoices.D: Rarity and age are of equal importance to a stamp's value.
answerChoices.E: Even old and rare stamps are usually not valuable if they are in poor condition.

stimulus: Leadership depends as much on making one's followers aware of their own importance as it does on conveying a vivid image of a collective goal. Only if they are convinced both that their efforts are necessary for the accomplishment of this goal, and that these efforts, if expended, will actually achieve it, will people follow a leader.
questionStem: If all of the statements above are true, then which one of the following cannot be true?

answerChoices.A: Some leaders who convince their followers of the necessity of their efforts in achieving a goal fail, nevertheless, to lead them to the attainment of that goal.
answerChoices.B: One who succeeds in conveying to one's followers the relationship between their efforts and the attainment of a collective goal succeeds in leading these people to this goal.
answerChoices.C: Only if one is a leader must one convince people of the necessity of their efforts for the attainment of a collective goal.
answerChoices.D: Sometimes people succeed in achieving a collective goal without ever having been convinced that by trying to do so they would succeed.
answerChoices.E: Sometimes people who remain unsure of whether their efforts are needed for the attainment of a collective goal nevertheless follow a leader.

stimulus: Fifty chronic insomniacs participated in a one-month study conducted at an institute for sleep disorders. Half were given a dose of a new drug and the other half were given a placebo every night before going to bed at the institute. Approximately 80 percent of the participants in each group reported significant relief from insomnia during the first two weeks of the study. But in each group, approximately 90 percent of those who had reported relief claimed that their insomnia had returned during the third week of the study.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain all the data from the study?

answerChoices.A: Because it is easy to build up a tolerance to the new drug, most people will no longer experience its effects after taking it every night for two weeks.
answerChoices.B: The psychological comfort afforded by the belief that one has taken a sleep-promoting drug is enough to prevent most episodes of insomnia.
answerChoices.C: The new drug is very similar in chemical composition to another drug, large doses of which have turned out to be less effective than expected.
answerChoices.D: Most insomniacs sleep better in a new environment, and the new drug has no effect on an insomniac's ability to sleep.
answerChoices.E: Some insomniacs cannot reliably determine how much sleep they have had or how well they have slept.

stimulus: Advertisement: The Country Classic is the only kind of car in its class that offers an antilock braking system that includes TrackAid. An antilock braking system keeps your wheels from locking up during hard braking, and TrackAid keeps your rear wheels from spinning on slippery surfaces. So if you are a safety-conscious person in the market for a car in this class, the Country Classic is the only car for you.
questionStem: The advertisement is misleading if which one of the following is true?

answerChoices.A: All of the cars that are in the same class as the Country Classic offer some kind of antilock braking system.
answerChoices.B: Most kinds of cars that are in the same class as the Country Classic are manufactured by the same company that manufactures the Country Classic.
answerChoices.C: Without an antilock braking system, the wheels of the Country Classic and other cars in its class are more likely to lock up during hard braking than they are to spin on slippery surfaces.
answerChoices.D: Other cars in the same class as the Country Classic offer an antilock braking system that uses a method other than TrackAid to prevent rear wheels from spinning on slippery surfaces.
answerChoices.E: The Country Classic is more expensive than any other car in its class.

stimulus: Sociologist: Traditional norms in our society prevent sincerity by requiring one to ignore unpleasant realities and tell small lies. But a community whose members do not trust one another cannot succeed. So, if a community is to succeed, its members must be willing to face unpleasant realities and speak about them honestly.
questionStem: The sociologist's conclusion follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: Sincerity is required if community members are to trust each other.
answerChoices.B: The more sincere and open community members are, the more likely that community is to succeed.
answerChoices.C: A community sometimes can succeed even if its members subscribe to traditional norms.
answerChoices.D: Unless a community's members are willing to face unpleasant realities, they cannot be sincere.
answerChoices.E: A community's failure is often caused by its members' unwillingness to face unpleasant realities and to discuss them honestly.

stimulus: Company president: Our consultants report that, in general, the most efficient managers have excellent time management skills. Thus, to improve productivity I recommend that we make available to our middle-level managers a seminar to train them in techniques of time management.
questionStem: Each of the following, if true, would weaken the support for the company president's recommendation except:

answerChoices.A: The consultants use the same criteria to evaluate managers' efficiency as they do to evaluate their time management skills.
answerChoices.B: Successful time management is more dependent on motivation than on good technique.
answerChoices.C: Most managers at other companies who have attended time management seminars are still unproductive.
answerChoices.D: Most managers who are already efficient do not need to improve their productivity.
answerChoices.E: Most managers who are efficient have never attended a time management seminar.

stimulus: Researcher: It is commonly believed that species belonging to the same biological order, such as rodents, descended from a single common ancestor. However, I compared the genetic pattern in 3 rodent species—guinea pigs, rats, and mice—as well as in 13 nonrodent mammals, and found that while rats and mice are genetically quite similar, the genetic differences between guinea pigs and mice are as great as those between mice and some nonrodent species. Thus, despite their similar physical form, guinea pigs stem from a separate ancestor.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously undermines the researcher's reasoning?

answerChoices.A: The researcher examined the genetic material of only 3 of over 2,000 species of rodents.
answerChoices.B: Some pairs of species not having a common ancestor are genetically more similar to each other than are some pairs that do have a common ancestor.
answerChoices.C: The researcher selected nonrodent species that have the specific cell structures she wanted to analyze genetically, though many nonrodent mammals lack these cell structures.
answerChoices.D: For some genuine biological orders, the most recent common ancestor dates from later epochs than does the most recent common ancestor of other biological orders.
answerChoices.E: Peculiarities of body structure, such as distinctive teeth and olfactory structures, are shared by all rodents, including guinea pigs.

stimulus: Industry experts expect improvements in job safety training to lead to safer work environments. A recent survey indicated, however, that for manufacturers who improved job safety training during the 1980s, the number of on-the-job accidents tended to increase in the months immediately following the changes in the training programs.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the passage above?

answerChoices.A: A similar survey found that the number of on-the-job accidents remained constant after job safety training in the transportation sector was improved.
answerChoices.B: Manufacturers tend to improve their job safety training only when they are increasing the size of their workforce.
answerChoices.C: Manufacturers tend to improve job safety training only after they have noticed that the number of on-the-job accidents has increased.
answerChoices.D: It is likely that the increase in the number of on-the-job accidents experienced by many companies was not merely a random fluctuation.
answerChoices.E: Significant safety measures, such as protective equipment and government safety inspections, were in place well before the improvements in job safety training.

stimulus: Two things are true of all immoral actions. First, if they are performed in public, they offend public sensibilities. Second, they are accompanied by feelings of guilt.
questionStem: If all of the statements above are true, then which one of the following must be false?

answerChoices.A: Some immoral actions that are not performed in public are not accompanied by feelings of guilt.
answerChoices.B: Immoral actions are wrong solely by virtue of being accompanied by feelings of guilt.
answerChoices.C: Some actions that offend public sensibilities if they are performed in public are not accompanied by feelings of guilt.
answerChoices.D: Some actions that are accompanied by feelings of guilt are not immoral, even if they frequently offend public sensibilities.
answerChoices.E: Every action performed in public that is accompanied by feelings of guilt is immoral.

stimulus: Vervet monkeys use different alarm calls to warn each other of nearby predators, depending on whether the danger comes from land or from the air.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, contributes most to an explanation of the behavior of vervet monkeys described above?

answerChoices.A: By varying the pitch of its alarm call, a vervet monkey can indicate the number of predators approaching.
answerChoices.B: Different land-based predators are responsible for different numbers of vervet monkey deaths.
answerChoices.C: No predators that pose a danger to vervet monkeys can attack both from land and from the air.
answerChoices.D: Vervet monkeys avoid land-based predators by climbing trees but avoid predation from the air by diving into foliage.
answerChoices.E: Certain land-based predators feed only on vervet monkeys, whereas every predator that attacks vervet monkeys from the air feeds on many different animals.

stimulus: Technological improvements will enable food production to increase as populations increase. However, increases in food production will be negligible unless societies become more centralized so that all factors contributing to the production of food can be better coordinated. But, historically, the more centralized a society was, the greater the percentage of its people who perished if and when it collapsed. Thus, increasing the centralization of societies in an effort to increase food production via better technology will merely exacerbate the disasters associated with societal collapse.
questionStem: The statements above, if true, most strongly support which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: The more centralized a society is, the greater its need for increased food production.
answerChoices.B: Not every problem associated with the collapse of a centralized society would be prevented by technological improvements.
answerChoices.C: The rate at which the world's population is growing will continue to increase indefinitely.
answerChoices.D: The production of food can be increased only by improved technology.
answerChoices.E: Societies have become more centralized as technology has improved.

stimulus: Statistical studies show that last year there was the greatest drop in the violent crime rate over the course of a year since such statistics were first gathered. But they also reveal that at the same time public anxiety about violent crime substantially increased.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy described above?

answerChoices.A: Longer prison sentences were the primary cause of the decrease in the violent crime rate over the course of last year.
answerChoices.B: As in the past, last year's increase in public anxiety about violent crime has been consistently underreported in the news media.
answerChoices.C: Most people can realistically assess the likelihood that they will become victims of violent crime.
answerChoices.D: People who feel the most anxiety about violent crime usually live in areas with relatively high violent crime rates.
answerChoices.E: The proportion of violent crimes covered in the news media nearly doubled over the course of last year.

stimulus: It is primarily by raising interest rates that central bankers curb inflation, but an increase in interest rates takes up to two years to affect inflation. Accordingly, central bankers usually try to raise interest rates before inflation becomes excessive, at which time inflation is not yet readily apparent either. But unless inflation is readily apparent, interest rate hikes generally will be perceived as needlessly restraining a growing economy. Thus, central bankers' success in temporarily restraining inflation may make it harder for them to ward off future inflation without incurring the public's wrath.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes the role played in the argument by the claim that it is primarily by raising interest rates that central bankers curb inflation?

answerChoices.A: It is presented as a complete explanation of the fact that central bankers' success in temporarily restraining inflation may make it harder for them to ward off future inflation without incurring the public's wrath.
answerChoices.B: It is a description of a phenomenon for which the claim that an increase in interest rates takes up to two years to affect inflation is offered as an explanation.
answerChoices.C: It is a premise offered in support of the conclusion that central bankers' success in temporarily restraining inflation may make it harder for them to ward off future inflation without incurring the public's wrath.
answerChoices.D: It is a conclusion for which the statement that an increase in interest rates takes up to two years to affect inflation is offered as support.
answerChoices.E: It is a premise offered in support of the conclusion that unless inflation is readily apparent, interest rate hikes generally will be perceived as needlessly restraining a growing economy.

stimulus: Environmentalist: Discarding old appliances can be dangerous: refrigerators contain chlorofluorocarbons; electronic circuit boards and cathode-ray tubes often contain heavy metals like lead; and old fluorescent bulbs contain mercury, another heavy metal. When landfills are operated properly, such materials pose no threat. However, when landfills are not operated properly, lead and mercury from them contaminate groundwater, for example. On the other hand, when trash is incinerated, heavy metals poison the ash and escape into the air.
questionStem: The environmentalist's statements, if true, most strongly support which one of the following inferences?

answerChoices.A: Old fluorescent bulbs should be recycled.
answerChoices.B: Appliances containing heavy metals should not be incinerated.
answerChoices.C: Chlorofluorocarbons are harmful to the atmosphere.
answerChoices.D: Newer appliances are more dangerous to the environment than older ones.
answerChoices.E: Appliances should be kept out of landfills.

stimulus: To be great, an artwork must express a deep emotion, such as sorrow or love. But an artwork cannot express an emotion that the artwork's creator is incapable of experiencing.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the statements above?

answerChoices.A: A computer can create an artwork that expresses sorrow or love only if it has actually experienced such an emotion.
answerChoices.B: The greatest art is produced by those who have experienced the deepest emotions.
answerChoices.C: An artwork that expresses a deep emotion of its creator is a great artwork.
answerChoices.D: As long as computers are constructed so as to be incapable of experiencing emotions they will not create great artworks.
answerChoices.E: Only artworks that succeed in expressing deep emotions are the products of great artists.

stimulus: Consumer activist: When antilock brakes were first introduced, it was claimed that they would significantly reduce the incidence of multiple-car collisions, thereby saving lives. Indeed, antilock brakes have reduced the incidence of multiple-car collisions. I maintain, however, that to save lives, automobile manufacturers ought to stop equipping cars with them.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent conflict in the consumer activist's statements?

answerChoices.A: Drivers and passengers in automobiles with antilock brakes feel less vulnerable, and are thus less likely to wear seat belts.
answerChoices.B: Under some circumstances, automobiles with traditional brakes stop just as quickly as do automobiles with antilock brakes.
answerChoices.C: For inexperienced drivers, antilock brakes are easier to use correctly than are traditional brakes.
answerChoices.D: Antilock brakes are considerably more expensive to manufacture than are traditional brakes.
answerChoices.E: Antilock brakes are no more effective in preventing multiple-car accidents than in preventing other kinds of traffic accidents.

stimulus: In older commercial airplanes, the design of the control panel allows any changes in flight controls made by one member of the flight crew to be immediately viewed by the other crew members. In recently manufactured aircraft, however, a crew member's flight control changes are harder to observe, thereby eliminating a routine means for performing valuable cross-checks. As a result, the flight crews operating recently manufactured airplanes must inform each other verbally about flight control changes much more frequently.
questionStem: The statements above, if true, most strongly support which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: How frequently an airplane's flight crew members will inform each other verbally about flight control changes depends in large part on how long it takes to perform those changes.
answerChoices.B: In recently manufactured aircraft, the most valuable means available for performing cross-checks involves frequent verbal exchanges of information among the flight crew members.
answerChoices.C: In older commercial airplanes, in contrast to recently manufactured airplanes, flight crew members have no need to exchange information verbally about flight control changes.
answerChoices.D: The flight crew members operating a recently manufactured airplane cannot observe the flight control changes made by other crew members by viewing the control panel.
answerChoices.E: How often flight crew members must share information verbally about flight control changes depends in part on what other means for performing cross-checks are available to the crew.

stimulus: According to the proposed Factory Safety Act, a company may operate an automobile factory only if that factory is registered as a class B factory. In addressing whether a factory may postpone its safety inspections, this Act also stipulates that no factory can be class B without punctual inspections. Thus, under the Factory Safety Act, a factory that manufactures automobiles would not be able to postpone its safety inspections.
questionStem: The argument proceeds by

answerChoices.A: pointing out how two provisions of the proposed Factory Safety Act jointly entail the unacceptability of a certain state of affairs
answerChoices.B: considering two possible interpretations of a proposed legal regulation and eliminating the less plausible one
answerChoices.C: showing that the terms of the proposed Factory Safety Act are incompatible with existing legislation
answerChoices.D: showing that two different provisions of the proposed Factory Safety Act conflict and thus cannot apply to a particular situation
answerChoices.E: pointing out that if a provision applies in a specific situation, it must apply in any analogous situation

stimulus: From the fact that people who studied music as children frequently are quite proficient at mathematics, it cannot be concluded that the skills required for mathematics are acquired by studying music: it is equally likely that proficiency in mathematics and studying music are both the result of growing up in a family that encourages its children to excel at all intellectual and artistic endeavors.
questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following arguments is most parallel to that in the argument above?

answerChoices.A: Although children who fail to pay attention tend to perform poorly in school, it should not necessarily be thought that their poor performance is caused by their failure to pay attention, for it is always possible that their failure to pay attention is due to undiagnosed hearing problems that can also lead to poor performance in school.
answerChoices.B: People who attend a university in a foreign country are usually among the top students from their native country. It would therefore be wrong to conclude from the fact that many foreign students perform better academically than others in this country that secondary schools in other countries are superior to those in this country; it may be that evaluation standards are different.
answerChoices.C: People whose diet includes relatively large quantities of certain fruits and vegetables have a slightly lower than average incidence of heart disease. But it would be premature to conclude that consuming these fruits and vegetables prevents heart disease, for this correlation may be merely coincidental.
answerChoices.D: Those who apply to medical school are required to study biology and chemistry. It would be a mistake, however, to conclude that those who have mastered chemistry and biology will succeed as physicians, for the practical application of knowledge is different from its acquisition.
answerChoices.E: Those who engage in vigorous exercise tend to be very healthy. But it would be silly to conclude that vigorous exercise is healthful simply because people who are healthy exercise vigorously, since it is possible that exercise that is less vigorous also has beneficial results.

stimulus: A physician has a duty to see to the health and best medical interests of the patient. On the other hand, the patient has a right to be fully informed about any negative findings concerning the patient's health. When this duty conflicts with this right, the right should prevail since it is a basic right. Anything else carries the risk of treating the patient as a mere object, not as a person.
questionStem: The conclusion drawn above follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: All persons have a right to accept or reject any medical procedures proposed by a physician.
answerChoices.B: Some actions are right independently of the consequences that might ensue.
answerChoices.C: Because only persons have rights, objects do not have rights.
answerChoices.D: A person's basic rights should never be violated.
answerChoices.E: In medicine, the patient's basic right to information is stronger than most other rights.

stimulus: Forester: The great majority of the forests remaining in the world are only sickly fragments of the fully functioning ecosystems they once were. These fragmented forest ecosystems have typically lost their ability to sustain themselves in the long term, yet they include the last refuges for some of the world's most endangered species. To maintain its full complement of plant and animal species, a fragmented forest requires regular interventions by resource managers.
questionStem: The forester's statements, if true, most strongly support which one of the following?

answerChoices.A: Most of the world's forests will lose at least some of their plant or animal species if no one intervenes.
answerChoices.B: Unless resource managers regularly intervene in most of the world's remaining forests, many of the world's most endangered species will not survive.
answerChoices.C: A fragmented forest ecosystem cannot sustain itself in the long term if it loses any of its plant or animal species.
answerChoices.D: A complete, fully functioning forest ecosystem can always maintain its full complement of plant and animal species even without interventions by resource managers.
answerChoices.E: At present, resource managers intervene regularly in only some of the world's fragmented forest ecosystems.

stimulus: Economist: Some people argue that when large countries split into several small countries, the world economy is harmed by increased barriers to free trade in the form of an increased number of national tariffs. But small countries do not think of themselves as economically self-sufficient. Therefore, such division of large countries does not increase barriers to free trade.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if assumed, enables the economist's conclusion to be properly drawn?

answerChoices.A: A country has the right to split into smaller countries even if some of the economic consequences of division would harm the world economy.
answerChoices.B: Increasing the number of countries in the world would strengthen rather than weaken the world economy.
answerChoices.C: All countries that impose national tariffs or other barriers to free trade think of themselves as economically self-sufficient.
answerChoices.D: There is strong evidence that national tariffs and other barriers to free trade harm the world economy.
answerChoices.E: Large countries tend to be more economically self-sufficient than small countries.

stimulus: During the nineteenth century, the French academy of art was a major financial sponsor of painting and sculpture in France; sponsorship by private individuals had decreased dramatically by this time. Because the academy discouraged innovation in the arts, there was little innovation in nineteenth century French sculpture. Yet nineteenth century French painting showed a remarkable degree of innovation.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the difference between the amount of innovation in French painting and the amount of innovation in French sculpture during the nineteenth century?

answerChoices.A: In France in the nineteenth century, the French academy gave more of its financial support to painting than it did to sculpture.
answerChoices.B: The French academy in the nineteenth century financially supported a greater number of sculptors than painters, but individual painters received more support, on average, than individual sculptors.
answerChoices.C: Because stone was so much more expensive than paint and canvas, far more unsponsored paintings were produced than were unsponsored sculptures in France during the nineteenth century.
answerChoices.D: Very few of the artists in France in the nineteenth century who produced sculptures also produced paintings.
answerChoices.E: Although the academy was the primary sponsor of sculpture and painting, the total amount of financial support that French sculptors and painters received from sponsors declined during the nineteenth century.

stimulus: People who consume a lot of honey tend to have fewer cavities than others have. Yet, honey is high in sugar, and sugar is one of the leading causes of tooth decay.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox described above?

answerChoices.A: People who eat a lot of honey tend to consume very little sugar from other sources.
answerChoices.B: Many people who consume a lot of honey consume much of it dissolved in drinks.
answerChoices.C: People's dental hygiene habits vary greatly.
answerChoices.D: Refined sugars have been linked to more health problems than have unrefined sugars.
answerChoices.E: Honey contains bacteria that inhibit the growth of the bacteria that cause tooth decay.

stimulus: Ethicist: The penalties for drunk driving are far more severe when the drunk driver accidentally injures people than when no one is injured. Moral responsibility for an action depends solely on the intentions underlying the action and not on the action's results. Therefore, legal responsibility, depending as it does in at least some cases on factors other than the agent's intentions, is different than moral responsibility.
questionStem: The claim that the penalties for drunk driving are far more severe when the drunk driver accidentally injures people than when no one is injured plays which one of the following roles in the ethicist's argument?

answerChoices.A: It is a premise offered in support of the claim that legal responsibility for an action is based solely upon features of the action that are generally unintended by the agent.
answerChoices.B: It is offered as an illustration of the claim that the criteria of legal responsibility for an action include but are not the same as those for moral responsibility.
answerChoices.C: It is offered as an illustration of the claim that people may be held morally responsible for an action for which they are not legally responsible.
answerChoices.D: It is a premise offered in support of the claim that legal responsibility depends in at least some cases on factors other than the agent's intentions.
answerChoices.E: It is a premise offered in support of the claim that moral responsibility depends solely on the intentions underlying the action and not on the action's result.

stimulus: Wood-frame houses withstand earthquakes far better than masonry houses do, because wooden frames have some flexibility; their walls can better handle lateral forces. In a recent earthquake, however, a wood-frame house was destroyed, while the masonry house next door was undamaged.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the results of the earthquake described above?

answerChoices.A: In earthquake-prone areas, there are many more wood-frame houses than masonry houses.
answerChoices.B: In earthquake-prone areas, there are many more masonry houses than wood-frame houses.
answerChoices.C: The walls of the wood-frame house had once been damaged in a flood.
answerChoices.D: The masonry house was far more expensive than the wood-frame house.
answerChoices.E: No structure is completely impervious to the destructive lateral forces exerted by earthquakes.

stimulus: The highest mountain ranges are formed by geological forces that raise the earth's crust: two continent-bearing tectonic plates of comparable density collide and crumple upward, causing a thickening of the crust. The erosive forces of wind and precipitation inexorably wear these mountains down. Yet the highest mountain ranges tend to be found in places where these erosive forces are most prevalent.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to reconcile the apparent conflict described above?

answerChoices.A: Patterns of extreme wind and precipitation often result from the dramatic differences in elevation commonly found in the highest mountain ranges.
answerChoices.B: The highest mountain ranges have less erosion-reducing vegetation near their peaks than do other mountain ranges.
answerChoices.C: Some lower mountain ranges are formed by a different collision process, whereby one tectonic plate simply slides beneath another of lesser density.
answerChoices.D: The amount of precipitation that a given region of the earth receives may vary considerably over the lifetime of an average mountain range.
answerChoices.E: The thickening of the earth's crust associated with the formation of the highest mountain ranges tends to cause the thickened portion of the crust to sink over time.

stimulus: In an experiment, volunteers witnessed a simulated crime. After they witnessed the simulation the volunteers were first questioned by a lawyer whose goal was to get them to testify inaccurately about the event. They were then cross-examined by another lawyer whose goal was to cause them to correct the inaccuracies in their testimony. The witnesses who gave testimony containing fewer inaccurate details than most of the other witnesses during the first lawyer's questioning also gave testimony containing a greater number of inaccurate details than most of the other witnesses during cross-examination.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent conflict in the results concerning the witnesses who gave testimony containing fewer inaccurate details during the first lawyer's questioning?

answerChoices.A: These witnesses were more observant about details than were most of the other witnesses.
answerChoices.B: These witnesses had better memories than did most of the other witnesses.
answerChoices.C: These witnesses were less inclined than most of the other witnesses to be influenced in their testimony by the nature of the questioning.
answerChoices.D: These witnesses were unclear about the details at first but then began to remember more accurately as they answered questions.
answerChoices.E: These witnesses tended to give testimony containing more details than most of the other witnesses.

stimulus: It is well documented that people have positive responses to some words, such as "kind" and "wonderful," and negative responses to others, such as "evil" and "nausea." Recently, psychological experiments have revealed that people also have positive or negative responses to many nonsense words. This shows that people's responses to words are conditioned not only by what the words mean, but also by how they sound.
questionStem: The claim that people have positive or negative responses to many nonsense words plays which one of the following roles in the argument?

answerChoices.A: It is a premise offered in support of the conclusion that people have either a positive or a negative response to any word.
answerChoices.B: It is a conclusion for which the only support provided is the claim that people's responses to words are conditioned both by what the words mean and by how they sound.
answerChoices.C: It is a generalization partially supported by the claim that meaningful words can trigger positive or negative responses in people.
answerChoices.D: It is a premise offered in support of the conclusion that people's responses to words are engendered not only by what the words mean, but also by how they sound.
answerChoices.E: It is a conclusion supported by the claim that people's responses under experimental conditions are essentially different from their responses in ordinary situations.

stimulus:
Larew: People in the lowest income quintile had a much higher percentage increase in average income over the last ten years than did those in the highest quintile. So their economic prosperity increased relative to the highest quintile's.
Mendota: I disagree. The average income for the lowest quintile may have increased by a greater percentage, but the absolute amount of the increase in average income was surely greater for the highest quintile.
questionStem: Larew and Mendota disagree about whether

answerChoices.A: change in the economic prosperity of the lowest income quintile relative to the highest is accurately measured by comparing their percentage changes in average income
answerChoices.B: change in the economic prosperity of the lowest income quintile is more accurately measured in terms relative to the highest income quintile than in terms relative only to the lowest income quintile
answerChoices.C: changes in the average income of people in the lowest quintile should ever be compared to changes in the average income of people in the highest quintile
answerChoices.D: there were any improvements at all in the economic situation of those in the lowest income quintile during the ten years being considered
answerChoices.E: the average income of people in the lowest quintile increased by a greater percentage over the last decade than did that of people in the highest quintile

stimulus: Researchers have found that, hours after birth, infants are able to distinguish faces from other images. Infants stare at drawings of faces for longer periods of time than they do at blank ovals or drawings in which facial features are scrambled.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the ability of newborn infants described above?

answerChoices.A: Certain abilities of facial pattern recognition are innate in humans, rather than learned.
answerChoices.B: The longer an infant stares at an object, the more interesting the infant finds that object.
answerChoices.C: Infants learn to associate human faces with the necessities of comfort and nourishment.
answerChoices.D: The less an infant stares at an object, the weaker the preference the infant has for that object.
answerChoices.E: Infants learn to associate the sound of human voices with the images of human faces.

stimulus: Essayist: Common sense, which is always progressing, is nothing but a collection of theories that have been tested over time and found useful. When alternative theories that prove even more useful are developed, they gradually take the place of theories already embodied in common sense. This causes common sense to progress, but, because it absorbs new theories slowly, it always contains some obsolete theories.
questionStem: If all of the essayist’s statements are true, then which one of the following must be true?

answerChoices.A: At least some new theories that have not yet been found to be more useful than any theory currently part of common sense will never be absorbed into the body of common sense.
