answerChoices.B: It takes for granted that any failure in an air bag’s computer control system will cause that air bag to inflate accidentally.
answerChoices.C: It fails to address adequately the possibility that air bags may often accidentally inflate even when their computer control systems do not fail.
answerChoices.D: It overlooks the possibility that, even if the new computer control systems exacerbate the problems with accidental air bag inflation, they may have advantages that outweigh this disadvantage.
answerChoices.E: It overlooks the possibility that, even if air bags occasionally cause accidental injuries, they may nonetheless be responsible for preventing many more injuries than they cause.

stimulus: Current evidence indicates that there is no methane on Planet 253. If that is the case, it is certain that there is no life on Planet 253. Since microbes always produce methane, if there is no methane then there are no microbes.
questionStem: The conclusion drawn above follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

answerChoices.A: There is, in fact, no methane on Planet 253.
answerChoices.B: If methane exists on Planet 253 then we would be able to detect its presence.
answerChoices.C: If there is no methane currently on Planet 253 then there has never been methane on Planet 253.
answerChoices.D: If there are no microbes on Planet 253 then there is no life on Planet 253.
answerChoices.E: If there is methane on Planet 253 then there must be life on Planet 253.

stimulus: When frightened by hunters in a truck, healthy gazelles run away quickly, efficiently using the landscape for concealment. But when a healthy gazelle detects the approach of a predator such as a lion, it leaps high into the air as it runs away—a behavior known as “stotting.” As a defensive behavior, stotting appears paradoxical, because it draws predators’ attention and consumes energy that could be put into running faster.
questionStem: Which one of the following would, if true, most help to resolve the apparent paradox described above?

answerChoices.A: Animals that are startled sometimes act in ways that appear irrational to human observers.
answerChoices.B: Young gazelles and gazelles that are not very healthy often stot when they become frightened by humans or by loud machines.
answerChoices.C: To animals that typically prey on gazelles, stotting is a signal of strength and ability to escape.
answerChoices.D: A healthy gazelle can usually detect the approach of a predator before the predator becomes aware of the presence of the gazelle.
answerChoices.E: While not able to run as quickly as gazelles, predators such as lions hunt effectively by hunting in groups and coordinating their attacks.

stimulus: To achieve the traditional hotness of spicy cuisines, cooks use some specific kind of chili or other spice. But, as experienced cooks know, if food is sufficiently spiced it is impossible to distinguish which ingredient is causing the hot sensation. Therefore, none of the hot spices traditionally used is irreplaceable.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

answerChoices.A: It is light-sensitive pigment in fishes’ eyes that makes it possible for them to see. Any one of a variety of pigments makes underwater vision possible. Therefore, no particular one of these pigments is necessary for underwater vision.
answerChoices.B: Every country needs an adequate defense. But this can be overdone; no country that devotes the majority of its resources to the military can avoid war. Therefore, peacetime cannot persist in any nation that uses over half of its resources to support its armed forces.
answerChoices.C: To receive a doctorate, a student must complete the required number of classes and write a dissertation. Therefore, any student who writes a dissertation and completes the required number of classes will receive a doctorate.
answerChoices.D: Attending a music concert is a far richer experience than listening to a recorded piece of music. When playing live, musicians often depart from the original score; therefore, each live concert is a unique and irreplaceable event.
answerChoices.E: Good cooks always select their ingredients carefully, for they know that every delicious meal is made with high-quality ingredients. Therefore, no meal made without high-quality ingredients is delicious.

stimulus:
A recent study has found that, surprisingly, the risk of
 serious injuries to workers is higher in industries that
 are monitored by government safety inspectors than in
 industries that are not so monitored.
questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain
 the surprising finding described above?

answerChoices.A: Government safety inspectors not only monitor but also train employees of the inspected firms to follow safe practices.
answerChoices.B: Government safety inspectors do not have the authority to enforce safety regulations.
answerChoices.C: Only those industries with an inherently high risk of on-the-job injury are monitored by government safety inspectors.
answerChoices.D: Workers behave especially cautiously when they believe their performance is being monitored by government safety inspectors.
answerChoices.E: Some of the industries that are monitored by government safety inspectors have much lower rates of injuries than do other industries that are also so monitored.

stimulus:
Historian: Scholars writing histories of an era’s business
 practices must, of course, analyze the practices
 and strategies employed by firms of that era.
 But historians probably study successful firms
 more frequently than they do unsuccessful firms.
 Therefore, it is reasonable to think that business
 histories overestimate the successes of past
 businesses.
questionStem:
Which one of the following would, if true, most support
 the historian’s argument?

answerChoices.A: The specific factors that cause businesses to do poorly are often not inferable from historical records of business activity.
answerChoices.B: Those who study past first-person accounts of business strategies inevitably approach them with certain present-day cultural assumptions.
answerChoices.C: The many public legal documents that firms have had to file provide a record that is more objective than that provided by the firms’ own internal documents.
answerChoices.D: The records of businesses that have gone bankrupt are destroyed more frequently than the records of other businesses.
answerChoices.E: Scholars who study businesses of the past are usually trained in the effective techniques of business administration. -32- 4 44

stimulus:
Committee chairperson: No new course will be approved
 for next year’s schedule unless a proposal for it has
 already been received either by this committee or
 by Dean Wilson. Dean Wilson has received only
 one new course proposal, and all of the new course
 proposals that this committee has received are
 for upper-level courses. It has been decided that,
 beginning next year, all upper-level courses will
 have prerequisites.
questionStem:
Which one of the following can be properly inferred if the
 chairperson’s statements are true?

answerChoices.A: If there are no new upper-level courses next year, then there will be no new courses next year that have prerequisites.
answerChoices.B: If all of the new courses next year are upper-level courses, then all of the new course proposals submitted to the committee will have been approved.
answerChoices.C: If there is more than one new course next year, at least one of them will be a course that has a prerequisite.
answerChoices.D: If the new course proposal that Dean Wilson received is for an upper-level course, then all courses offered next year will have prerequisites.
answerChoices.E: If there are no new upper-level courses next year, then the new course proposal that was submitted to Dean Wilson will have been approved. -17- 22 2

stimulus:
Consumer demand for personal computers continues to
 increase each year, which might lead one to think that
 the profits earned selling personal computers at the retail
 level are very high relative to total retail sales of personal
 computers. Yet the retail profit margin on personal
 computer sales is extremely low compared to that of
 other popular high-technology items.
questionStem:
Each of the following, if true, helps to resolve the
 apparent discrepancy described above except:

answerChoices.A: Rapid innovation in computer technology increases the likelihood of a store’s stock becoming obsolete.
answerChoices.B: Satisfaction with their first personal computer tends to make customers very loyal to that particular brand.
answerChoices.C: A customer needs more help from store employees when buying a personal computer than when buying other high-technology items.
answerChoices.D: Many retail stores have low prices on personal computers in order to bring in customers who might buy software and accessories.
answerChoices.E: An increase in the number of discount retail outlets selling personal computers has intensified the competition for customers.

stimulus:
Superstring theory is a controversial new theory in
 physics that purports, unlike more established physical
 theories, to explain the nature and existence of gravity.
 A major problem with superstring theory is that to test it
 we would have to build a particle accelerator 100 trillion
 kilometers long. Another problem is that superstring
 theory has had no success in adequately explaining why
 the force of gravity is not stronger or weaker than it is.
questionStem:
Which one of the following is most strongly supported
 by the information above?

answerChoices.A: Superstring theory would be more successful if superstring theorists attempted to explain why the force of gravity is not stronger or weaker than it is.
answerChoices.B: Physical theories that are better established than superstring theory provide better explanations of physical phenomena than does superstring theory.
answerChoices.C: Some physical theory more established than superstring theory has had at least some success in explaining why the force of gravity is not stronger or weaker than it is.
answerChoices.D: A physical theory cannot be true if testing that theory would require us to build a particle accelerator 100 trillion kilometers long.
answerChoices.E: A theory that purports to explain the nature of a force is deficient if it cannot account for the strength of that force.

stimulus:
On the plains where it lives, an individual zebra stands
 out because of its black-and-white stripes, which contrast
 with the green or brown of the surrounding vegetation.
 Yet zebras are a prey species, and the lions that hunt them
 can see stripes clearly. It seems surprising that zebras
 would survive with such vivid markings.
questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most adequately
 resolves the problem raised above?

answerChoices.A: Because the vegetation on the open plains changes from green to brown as the season changes from wet to dry, true camouflage coloring for a prey species would have to change according to the seasons.
answerChoices.B: Zebras are able to judge from the demeanor of lions they see in the vicinity whether or not those lions are preparing to hunt, and the zebras ignore the lions that are not.
answerChoices.C: Lions that hunt zebras are themselves colored in a way that blends in with the brown color of dry vegetation, so that in the dry season, when prey is scarce, the lions can creep up on their prey to within a distance from which the lions have a favorable chance of succeeding in the hunt.
answerChoices.D: When lions hunt, the whole pride shares in the food obtained when a prey animal is successfully brought down by one of the hunting lions.
answerChoices.E: When zebras run in a group, as they generally do in response to danger, the stripe markings make it difficult for a predator pursuing a single individual to discern its outline. -13- 22 2

stimulus:
Surprisingly, a new study has revealed that shortly after a
 heavy rainfall, pollution levels in Crystal Bay reach their
 highest levels. This occurs despite the fact that rainwater
 is almost totally pure and one would therefore expect that
 it would dilute the polluted seawater.
questionStem:
Which one of the following, if true, most helps to
 explain why pollution levels in Crystal Bay increase
 after a heavy rainfall?

answerChoices.A: Compared to the total amount of polluted seawater, the amount of rainwater that falls into Crystal Bay is negligible.
answerChoices.B: Most of the rainwater that eventually reaches Crystal Bay falls on pesticide-treated fields before being carried into the bay.
answerChoices.C: Most rainwater carried by clouds consists of water that has evaporated from oceans around the world.
answerChoices.D: The single leading cause of pollution in Crystal Bay is beachgoers’ leaving behind their trash and debris, which then blows into the bay.
answerChoices.E: Other nearby ocean areas experience a pattern of pollutant increase and decrease that is extremely similar to that of Crystal Bay. -22- 3 33

stimulus:
The study of primates is interesting for many reasons,
 including the fact that only primates have opposable
 thumbs. The lemurs are lower primates and the only
 primates indigenous to Madagascar, a large island off the
 coast of southeastern Africa. Some species of lemurs are
 the only living lower primates that are diurnal—that is,
 active primarily during the day. All higher primates are
 thought to have evolved from a single diurnal species of
 lower primates.
questionStem:
Which one of the following can be properly inferred
 from the information above?

answerChoices.A: The chimpanzee, a higher primate, evolved from the lemur.
answerChoices.B: No primates indigenous to Madagascar are diurnal higher primates.
answerChoices.C: No higher primate is nocturnal.
answerChoices.D: There are some lemurs without opposable thumbs.
answerChoices.E: There are no nocturnal lemurs. -26- 3 33

stimulus: A process of extracting caffeine from coffee without seriously compromising the coffee’s taste was introduced a number of years ago. When this decaffeinated coffee first came on the market, however, many coffee drinkers reported that it tasted rather bad.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the statements above?

answerChoices.A: The percentage of coffee drinkers who drink only decaffeinated coffee is much larger today than it was at the time the process was introduced.
answerChoices.B: Many coffee drinkers would not drink decaffeinated coffee even if they believed that it tasted as good as regular coffee.
answerChoices.C: The taste of any kind of coffee can be affected by the foods that are consumed along with it.
answerChoices.D: Coffee that is decaffeinated through this process generally costs more than regular coffee.
answerChoices.E: During the years in which the process was introduced, coffee processors used only low-quality coffee beans for their decaffeinated products.

stimulus: Market studies confirm that consumers shopping for automobiles primarily seek those that are most reliable. An automobile is reliable if it very rarely breaks down and it does not require significantly more maintenance than average. Strangely enough, however, some of the most reliable models do not sell well with those who say they care most about reliability.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

answerChoices.A: Consumers who are shopping for an automobile claim to care more about reliability than about fuel efficiency.
answerChoices.B: Consumers often choose automobile models based on a reputation for reliability, and reputations can be out of date.
answerChoices.C: Some owners of reliable automobiles are reluctant to trade them in for newer vehicles and tend to hold on to them for the life of the automobile.
answerChoices.D: Some automobile models that have been shown to require a lot of maintenance very rarely break down.
answerChoices.E: Some of the most stylish automobiles are some of the most unreliable.

stimulus: Environmentalist: The adoption of genetically engineered crops in agriculture is moving so rapidly and is monitored so loosely that it poses a significant risk of damaging sensitive ecosystems. One such crop had already been widely planted when a study found that it could threaten monarch butterflies. Therefore, before any new genetically engineered crop is put into agricultural production, rigorous testing of its safety should be required.
questionStem: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the environmentalist’s reasoning?

answerChoices.A: A genetically engineered crop should not be put into agricultural production if rigorous testing has shown it to be risky.
answerChoices.B: If a crop has no potential for posing environmental risks, it may be put into agricultural production without testing of its safety.
answerChoices.C: No crop that might present risks to the environment should be allowed into agricultural production unless its safety has been thoroughly tested.
answerChoices.D: If rigorous testing of any genetically engineered crop that is in agricultural production shows that that crop poses environmental risks, production of that crop should be discontinued.

stimulus: A tiny crab that lives 550 meters below the surface of the Gulf of Mexico has been found to have eyes that are sensitive to ultraviolet light. But ultraviolet light from the sun cannot penetrate to that depth. If the crab’s ultraviolet receptors developed as an adaptation to the depths, they are probably for detecting light from bioluminescent organisms. In that case, since the crab is not itself bioluminescent, it probably hunts bioluminescent prey.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, would most weaken the argument?

answerChoices.A: A trait that serves no function tends to be lost over time.
answerChoices.B: Prey is not plentiful at the depth at which the crabs are found.
answerChoices.C: The crabs can detect each other by nonvisual means.
answerChoices.D: It takes many generations to develop sensitivity to ultraviolet light.
answerChoices.E: The crab’s most dangerous predators are bioluminescent.

stimulus: Last year a local advertising agency produced many of its television commercials in a studio with improperly installed equipment. As a result, the sound in these commercials was not perfectly synchronized with the picture; this was particularly noticeable when people were shown talking, and it even prompted complaints from some viewers. However, local automobile dealerships that relied on television commercials from this agency tended to have greater sales increases during this period than did local dealerships using television commercials from other agencies instead.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the sales discrepancy described above?

answerChoices.A: Most viewers turned off the sound on their televisions when local automobile-dealership commercials aired during this period.
answerChoices.B: People are more likely to recall a television commercial they have seen if the sound and pictures were not properly synchronized.
answerChoices.C: Most of the advertisers that relied on commercials produced at the studio with improperly installed equipment were automobile dealerships.
answerChoices.D: Not all of the commercials produced for automobile dealerships at this studio contained video of people talking.
answerChoices.E: Most of the local automobile dealerships during this time did not rely heavily on television advertising.
